Zoning Resolution for Genoa Township
Delaware County, Ohio
EFFECTIVE MAY 14, 2026
Published by:
American Legal Publishing
525 Vine Street, Suite 310
Cincinnati, Ohio 45202
Tel: (800) 445-5588
Internet: http://www.amlegal.com
 
WHEREAS, the Board of Trustees of Genoa Township, Delaware County, Ohio (the
Board) has deemed it necessary to promote the public health, safety, morals,
and general welfare of the residents of said Township (the Township); and,
WHEREAS, in accordance with Ohio Revised Code Section 519.04 and 519.13, five
(5) persons have been duly appointed by the Board to serve as a Zoning
Commission for the Township, and five (5) other persons have been duly
appointed by the Board to serve as a Board of Zoning Appeals for the Township;
and,
WHEREAS, Zoning Resolutions for the building and land use within the
unincorporated territory of the Township were adopted in 1951 (East) and 1956
(West) in accordance with Section 519 and related sections of the Ohio Revised
Code; were amended in 1969 and 1971, respectively, and were thereafter merged
into a singular Zoning Resolution, on October 20, 1987, effective November 19,
1987, and subsequently amended on numerous occasions thereafter; and,
WHEREAS, the Board adopted a Comprehensive Plan in 1999 and subsequently
updated and revised said Plan in 2008, 2009, 2016, 2019, and 2023: and,
WHEREAS, the Board has amended this Zoning Resolution on numerous occasions
since 1999 in accordance with said Plan per Ohio Revised Code 519.02: and,
WHEREAS, the Board most recently adopted amendments to the October 20, 2022,
Zoning Resolution under the authority of, and in accordance with, the
provisions of the Ohio Revised Code, with said amendments becoming effective:
May 20, 2023; and,
WHEREAS, the Zoning Commission has recommended revisions of the Genoa Township
Zoning Resolution on June 9, 2025, and has submitted such amendments to the
Board under authority of, and in accordance with, the provisions of Section
519.12 of the Ohio Revised Code; and,
THEREFORE, the Board adopts amendments to this Zoning Resolution under the
authority of, and in accordance with, the provisions of the Ohio Revised Code,
with said amendments becoming effective: May 14, 2026; and,
FURTHERMORE, all resolutions or parts of resolutions in conflict with this
Zoning Resolution or inconsistent with provisions of this Resolution are hereby
repealed to the extent necessary to give this Resolution full force and effect.
 
APPROVED BY:
Genoa Township Board of Trustees
April 14, 2026
ARTICLE 1: Administration
Section 101: Title
101.01   This Resolution, including the official Zoning District Map (e.g.,
“Genoa Township Zoning Map”, “Zoning Map ”, etc.) made a part hereof as further
detailed Article
5, Section
502, shall be known and may be referred to or cited as the “Genoa Township
Zoning Resolution” (e.g., “this Resolution”, “this Zoning Resolution”).
Section 102: General Authority and Jurisdiction
102.01   Per Ohio Revised Code (ORC) Section 519.02, except as otherwise
provided in ORC 519, in the interest of the public health, safety, and general
welfare, the Township Trustees may regulate by resolution, in accordance with a
Comprehensive Plan , the location, Height , bulk, number of stories, and size
of Building s and other Structure s, including tents, cabins, and trailer
coaches, percentages of Lot Area s that may be occupied, Setback  Building
lines, sizes of Yards, courts, and other Open Spaces, the density of
population, the Use s of Building s and other Structure s, including tents,
cabins, and trailer coaches, and the Use s of land for trade, industry,
residence, recreation, or other purposes in the unincorporated territory of
Genoa Township. Furthermore, except as otherwise provided in ORC 519, in the
interest of the public convenience, comfort, prosperity, or general welfare,
the Township Trustees by resolution, in accordance with a Comprehensive Plan ,
may regulate the Setback lines for, and the Use s of Building s and other
Structure s, including tents cabins, and trailer coaches, and the Use s for
trade, industry, residence, recreation, or other purposes in the unincorporated
territory of Genoa Township and may establish reasonable residential
landscaping standards and residential architectural standards, excluding
exterior building materials, for the unincorporated territory of Genoa
Township. Additionally, except as otherwise provided in ORC 519, in the
interest of public convenience, comfort, property, or general welfare, the
Township Trustees may regulate by resolution, in accordance with a
Comprehensive Plan , for nonresidential property only, the Height , bulk,
number of stores, and size of Building s and other Structure s, including
tents, cabins, and trailer coaches, percentages of Lot Area s that may be
occupied, sizes of Yards, courts, and other Open Spaces, and the Density of
population in the unincorporated territory of Genoa Township. For all these
purposes, the Township Trustees may divide all or any part of the
unincorporated territory of Genoa Township into (Zoning) Districts or zones of
such number, shape, and area as the Trustees determines. All such regulations
shall be uniform for each class or kind of Building or other Structure or Use
throughout any District or zone, but the regulations in one District or zone
may differ from those in other (Zoning) Districts or zones.
   A)   For any activities permitted and regulated under ORC Chapters 1513
(coal surface mining) or 1514 (other surface mining) and any related processing
activities, the Township Trustees may regulate under the authority conferred by
ORC Section 519.02 only in the interest of public health and safety.
   B)   Pursuant to ORC 519.02.B, the Township Trustees may modify
administrative zoning procedures concerning adult entertainment establishments,
defined in ORC 2907.39, as they determine necessary to ensure that the
procedures comply with all applicable constitutional requirements.
   C)   The Township shall retain any and all zoning authority, jurisdiction,
and/or power granted to it by the ORC . The failure to accurately cite or
recite, in whole or in part, any such authority, jurisdiction, and/or power
within this Zoning Resolution shall not be considered, understood, construed,
or interpreted as abandonment or relinquishment of such authority,
jurisdiction, or power.
102.02   The provisions of this Resolution shall apply to all lands, Building
s, Structure s, Sign s, Swimming Pool s, and/or Use s within the unincorporated
area of Genoa Township, Delaware County, Ohio unless otherwise specified herein
or exempted by the ORC or by any other law or governing agency with
jurisdiction or authority over such matter.
102.03   Agriculture , viticulture, dairying, animal/poultry, husbandry, and
other such Use s recognized by the ORC shall be permitted in accordance with
ORC 519.01 and 519.21 as well as the standards set forth in Section
2302 of this Resolution, as may be amended.
102.04   Agritourism shall be permitted in accordance with ORC 901.80 and
519.21(C)(4) as well as the standards set forth in Section
2303, as may be amended.
102.05   Farm Market s shall be permitted in accordance with ORC 519.21(C)(1)
and the standards set forth in Section
2304, as may be amended.
102.06   Public Utilities and Railroads. In accordance with ORC 519.211, public
utilities and railroads shall not be prohibited in respect to the location,
erecting, construction , reconstruction, change, Alteration , maintenance,
removal, use, or enlargement of any Building s or Structure s for the operation
of its business except as otherwise provided for telecommunication towers in
Section
2204 of this Zoning Resolution.
102.07   Governmental Facilities . Any local, state, or federal governmental
Use shall not be prohibited in any Zoning District . Such local, state, or
federal governmental bodies proposing a Use of land or the construction of a
Structure incidental to their governmental functions and responsibilities shall
make a good faith effort to comply with this Zoning Resolution.
102.08   Sale or Use of Alcoholic Beverages. In accordance with ORC 519.211.D,
the sale or use of alcoholic beverages shall not be prohibited in areas where
the establishment and operation of any Retail business, Hotel , lunchroom, or
Restaurant is permitted.
102.09   Outdoor Advertising . In accordance with ORC 519.20, outdoor
advertising shall be classified as a business Use and shall be permitted in all
Districts zoned for industry, business, trade, or lands used for agricultural
purposes. Outdoor advertising shall comply with all applicable provisions
within Article
18 of this Resolution.
102.10   Oil and Gas Production . In accordance with ORC 1509.02, the
permitting, location, and spacing of oil and gas wells and production
operations shall fall under the authority of the Ohio Department of Natural
Resources’ Division of Oil and Gas Resources.
102.11   Biodiesel and Energy Production. In accordance with ORC 519.21(C)(2),
biodiesel production , biomass energy production , or electric or heat energy
production where the land on which the production facility is located qualifies
as land devoted exclusively to agricultural use under ORC Sections 5713.30 to
5713.37 for real property tax purposes shall be a permitted Use in all Zoning
Districts .
102.12   Biologically Derived Methane Gas Production. In accordance with ORC
519.21(C)(3), biologically derived methane gas production where the land on
which the production facility is located qualifies as land devoted exclusively
to agricultural use under Sections 5173.30 to 5713.37 for real property tax
purposes shall be a permitted Use in all Zoning Districts so long as the
facility that produces the biologically derived methane gas does not produce
more than seventeen million sixty thousand seven hundred ten (17,060,710)
British thermal units, five (5) megawatts, or both.
102.13   Marijuana Medical or Otherwise. In accordance with ORC 519.21(D),
3780, and 3796, Genoa Township reserves the right to, via this Resolution and/
or a separate resolution, prohibit medical marijuana , cultivators, processors,
and/or retail dispensaries, as well as adult use cannabis operators, from being
located within the unincorporated territory of the township as well the right
to regulate the location of said facilities within the aforementioned area.
102.14   Permanently Sited Manufactured Homes shall be permitted in any Zoning
District where a single-family home is permitted in accordance with ORC 519.212
but are subject to regulation as authorized by the aforementioned code section.
102.15   Solar and Wind Farms .
   A)   Small Solar Facilities shall be permitted in accordance with ORC
519.213 and the standards set forth in this Zoning Resolution, including
Articles
4,
5, and
22, as may be amended.
   B)   Small Wind Farms shall be permitted in accordance with ORC 519.213 and
the standards set forth in this Zoning Resolution, including Articles
4,
5, and
22, as may be amended.
102.16   Amateur radio service communications and structures. In accordance
with ORC 519.214, Genoa Township shall comply with ORC 5502.031 regarding the
regulation of amateur radio service communications and structures.
Section 103: Intent and Purpose
103.01   This is a Zoning Resolution for Genoa Township, Delaware County, Ohio,
adopted and amended pursuant to Chapter 519 of the ORC for the following
purposes, among others:
   A)   To promote and protect the health, safety, morals, and general welfare
of the present and future inhabitants of Genoa Township while protecting the
property rights of all residents.
   B)   To protect the quality of life through the protection of the total
environment, the prevention of Nuisance s and hazards, and the provision of
adequate light, air, and convenient access to property.
   C)   To ensure the compatibility of land Use s which are either adjacent or
in proximity to each other.
   D)   To promote, ensure, and control the orderly development of all lands
within the Township to its appropriate Use .
   E)   To promote and secure the most appropriate Use of land to facilitate
and provide adequate public and private improvements.
   F)   To conserve and protect the natural resources, scenic areas, wildlife
habitat and the historical and unique natural features of the land.
   G)   To recognize and to protect the right to farm all suitable land in
Genoa Township as further prescribed in Sections
102.03,
102.04,
102.05,
2302,
2303, and
2304 of this Resolution.
   H)   To implement the recommendations of the Genoa Township Comprehensive
Plan .
Section 104: Interpretation
104.01   In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this
Resolution shall be held to be minimum requirements, adopted for the promotion
of the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare.
   A)   Whenever the requirements of this Resolution conflict with itself, the
stricter, higher standard shall apply. Whenever the requirements of this
Resolution conflict with the ORC , the ORC shall prevail.
   B)   Where this Zoning Resolution imposes a greater restriction than is
imposed or required by other provisions of law or by other rules, regulations,
or resolutions, the provisions of this Zoning Resolution shall control,
provided it does not conflict with the ORC or federal law.
104.02   It is not the intention of this Resolution to interfere with,
abrogate, or annul any resolutions, ordinances, rules, regulations, or permits
previously adopted or issued, and not in conflict with any of the provisions of
this Resolution, or which shall be adopted or issued, pursuant to the Use of
Building or premises and likewise not in conflict with this Resolution; nor is
it intended by this Resolution to interfere, abrogate, or annul any Right-of-
Ways, easements, covenants, or other agreements between parties; subject to
Section
104.01 as may be amended.
104.03   This Zoning Resolution shall be interpreted and administered in a
manner consistent with the United States Constitution and all amendments
thereof, including the First Amendment guarantee of free speech, as well as the
Ohio Constitution, Ohio Revised Code, and any other applicable laws, federal,
state, or otherwise.
104.04   The “Intent and Purpose” (sub)sections of this and all other articles
within this Resolution primarily act as a guide that set forth goals and
objectives rather than a directly enforceable regulation in itself.
Section 105: Construction of Language
105.01   Definitions of words and terms are set forth in Article
4.
105.02   Terms or words shall be construed as follows:
   A)   Singular includes the plural, and the plural the singular.
   B)   Present tense shall include the future tense.
   C)   The word “shall” is mandatory; ”may” is permissive.
   D)   “Used for” shall include, but is not limited to, the phrases “arranged
for,” “designed for,” “intended for,” “maintained for,” and “occupied for.”
   E)   “Person” includes entities as well as an individual.
   F)   Unless the context clearly suggests to the contrary, conjunctions shall
be interpreted as follows:
      1)   “And” indicates that all connected items, conditions, provisions, or
events shall apply.
      2)   “Or” indicates that one or more of the connected items, conditions,
provisions, or events shall apply.
   G)   Lists with “including” or similar language are intended to provide
examples and are not exhaustive.
   H)   Specific provisions control over the general ones.
105.03   All times shall be Eastern Time (ET) and in twelve (12) hour format
(e.g., 1:00 p.m.).
Section 106: Separability
106.01   If for any reason any portion(s) of this Zoning Resolution shall be
declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unconstitutional or
invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair or invalidate the remaining
provisions of this Zoning Resolution, but shall be confined in its operation to
the specific portion(s) of this Zoning Resolution held invalid, and the
invalidity of any portion(s) of this Zoning Resolution in one or more instances
shall not affect or prejudice in any way the validity of this Zoning Resolution
in any other instance.
Section 107: Required Conformance
107.01   Except as herein provided and within Section
117, no Building , Structure , Sign , Swimming Pool , land, or site shall be
erected, converted, enlarged, improved, reconstructed, moved, structurally
altered, used, or otherwise modified, unless it is in compliance and
conformance with all applicable standards of this Zoning Resolution and/or any
valid Legal Approval (s).
107.02   Amendments to this Zoning Resolution shall not apply to any Zoning Map
Amendment or Legal Approval applied for, or granted, prior to the effective
date of the amendment and such situations shall be subject to Article
25, Non-Conformities. Amendments shall apply when:
   A)   A Zoning Map Amendment application is submitted on or after the
amendment’s effective date;
   B)   Legal Approval applications, including Final Development Plan
applications, are submitted on or after the amendment’s effective date; or
   C)   An application submitted on or after the amendment’s effective date
seeks to alter, revise, change, or amend a previously granted Zoning Map
Amendment or Legal Approval , including Final Development Plans. Unless
otherwise stated, amendments apply to applications submitted on or after their
effective date.
107.03   The burden of demonstrating that an application, development, or Use
of land or Structure s subject to this Resolution complies with applicable
review and approval standards or is a legal nonconformity subject to Article
25 is on the applicant, property owner, etc., as opposed to the Township or
other parties.
Section 108: Comprehensive Plan
108.01   Legislative amendments to this Zoning Resolution shall be consistent
with the Genoa Township Comprehensive Plan . The Comprehensive Plan may be
utilized as a guide in the administration of this Zoning Resolution. In
instances of conflict, the Zoning Resolution shall control.
Section 109: Validity of Citations and References
109.01   All article and section citations within this Zoning Resolution shall
be assumed to be referring to this Resolution unless otherwise expressly
stated, implied, inferred, or in any other way made obvious.
109.02   References to the ORC , Ohio Administrative Code (OAC), or any other
acts, laws, and/or plans text external to this Resolution, reflect their status
as of the date of the Resolution’s adoption. Whenever any provision of this
Resolution references such and it is later amended or superseded, this
Resolution shall be deemed amended to refer to the amended section or the
section that most nearly corresponds to the superseded section. Subsequent
amendments, re-numberings, or revisions of this Resolution shall not invalidate
such references.
109.03   Any change in the name, authority, or responsibility of a governmental
or regulatory agency referenced herein or the establishment of a successor
agency shall not affect the validity of this Resolution.
Section 110: Reserved
Section 111: Reserved
Section 112: Township Trustees
112.01   In accordance with the ORC , including ORC 519.16, and this
Resolution, the Township Trustees shall be responsible for:
   A)   Appointment and removal of the Zoning Inspector, Zoning Secretary,
zoning staff, members of the Genoa Township Zoning Commission , members of the
Genoa Township Board of Zoning Appeals , and, if so established, members of the
Genoa Township Architectural Review Board.
   B)   Provisions for a system of zoning certificates and may provide
disbursements necessary for enforcement of this Resolution.
   C)   Establishment of a schedule of fees to defray the costs of
administering and enforcing this Zoning Resolution.
   D)   Consideration of, and adoption, rejection, or modification of, proposed
amendments to this Resolution, including the Zoning Map , in accordance with
ORC 519.12 and Article
26 of this Resolution.
   E)   Consideration of, and adoption, rejection, or modification of, proposed
Final Development Plan s and Final Development Plan amendments as provided in
Article
27.
   F)   Other duties as may be specified within this Resolution.
112.02   It is the intent of this Resolution that all questions of
interpretation and enforcement shall be first presented to the Township Zoning
Inspector. Appeals from a decision of the Zoning Inspector shall be heard
exclusively the BZA pursuant to Article
3, Section
306 of this Resolution. Further, it is the intent of this Resolution that any
recourse from decisions of the BZA shall be pursued through the courts as
provided by law. The duties of the Township Trustees under this Resolution
shall not include hearing or deciding questions of interpretation and
enforcement, except as specifically authorized herein. This limitation shall
not apply to the administrative review of applications presented to the
Township Trustees for consideration in accordance with this Resolution.
Section 113: Classification of Actions
113.01   The approval of a Zoning Map Amendment shall be considered a
legislative action subject to referendum pursuant to ORC 3519.01.
113.02   The approval or denial of a Final Development Plan , including any
amendment thereto, shall constitute an administrative action.
113.03   The approval or denial of a Zoning Permit , the issuance or
withholding of a Certificate of Compliance , and any other ministerial action
taken by the Zoning Inspector or their designee shall constitute administrative
actions.
113.04   The approval or denial of a Variance or Conditional Use application,
as well as the decision rendered in an Administrative Appeal case, shall
constitute quasi-judicial actions.
Section 114: Administrative Bodies and Duties
114.01   Pursuant to ORC 519.16 and 519.161, the Township Trustees may appoint
a Township Zoning Inspector and assistants as deemed necessary. The Zoning
Inspector shall serve as the primary administrator and enforcement officer of
this Resolution and may exercise reasonable discretion in limited circumstances
to protect the public interest. Township officials and employees may assist the
Zoning Inspector by reporting any new construction , reconstruction, land Use
changes, or suspected violation. Duties of the Zoning Inspector shall include,
but are not necessarily limited to:
   A)   Reviewing all Zoning Permit applications as outlined in Section
115.01 to ensure compliance with this Resolution and maintaining related
records.
   B)   Reviewing all applications for Zoning Map Amendment s, zoning text
amendments, Final Development Plan s, Final Development Plan amendments,
Variance s, Conditional Use s, and Administrative Appeals and reporting
findings to the appropriate body.
   C)   Conducting site inspections within the purview of applicable laws and
legal guidance to ensure the zoning-related activities conform to applicable
Legal Approvals.
   D)   Issuing written notice of zoning violations and ordering corrective
action when sufficient evidence of non-compliance exists, subject to legal
guidance.
   E)   Ordering discontinuance of unlawful land Use s, Building s, or
Structure s in accordance with the provisions of the ORC .
   F)   Ordering removal of illegal Building s or Structure s or illegal
additions or structural Alterations in accordance with the provisions of the
ORC .
   G)   Reviewing subdivision plats and lot splits submitted to the Delaware
County Regional Planning Commission to determine if the plat or lot split
conforms to applicable provisions of this Resolution.
   H)   Maintaining records regarding the administration and enforcement of
this Zoning Resolution in accordance with the Township’s Public Records Policy
and the Township’s Records Retention Schedule in effect.
   I)   Providing reports to the Zoning Commission , Board of Zoning Appeals ,
and/or Township Trustees regarding enforcement and administrative activities.
   J)   Interpreting and making administrative determinations regarding this
Zoning Resolution, subject to appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals as set
forth in Article
3, unless reserved for another body.
   K)   Establishing and amending administrative procedures, forms, schedules,
and other such ministerial items necessary for lawful administration subject to
Township Trustees review. Zoning fee schedules shall require Township Trustees
approval.
   L)   Consulting with legal counsel, as needed, regarding zoning
administration and enforcement.
   M)   Exercising all authority expressly granted by this Zoning Resolution.
   N)   Delegating duties to authorized personnel assisting with zoning
administration and enforcement.
   O)   Managing resources allocated by the Township Trustees for zoning
administration and enforcement.
   P)   Performing other duties or responsibilities as prescribed by this
Zoning Resolution or the Township Trustees .
114.02   To assist in administrating the Zoning Resolution, pursuant to ORC
519.16, the Township Trustees shall appoint a Zoning Secretary responsible for
maintaining zoning records, verifying application information, processing
required public notices, recording the minutes of the Zoning Commission and
Board of Zoning Appeals , assisting the Zoning Inspector, and performing other
related duties as directed by the Township Trustees . The Township Fiscal
Officer may serve as the Zoning Secretary and may receive compensation for such
services in addition to other compensation allowed by law.
114.03   Whenever a provision appears requiring the Zoning Inspector or any
other official working for or under the Township Trustees to perform an act or
duty, that provision shall be construed as authorizing the delegation of such
responsibility to subordinates, unless the provisions herein this Resolution or
applicable law specify otherwise.
Section 115: Zoning Permit s and Certificates of Compliance
115.01   No person shall establish or change any Use of land, nor shall they
locate, erect, construct, reconstruct, enlarge, or structurally alter any
Building , Structure , Sign , and/or Swimming Pool within Genoa Township,
without first obtaining a Zoning Permit , subject to the following:
   A)   No Zoning Permit shall be issued unless the plans for the proposed
project fully comply with the provisions of this Resolution except where the
Zoning Inspector receives a written order from the BZA deciding an appeal, a
Variance , or Conditional Use .
   B)   A Zoning Permit shall be required for all Dwelling s, Principal
Structure s and Use s, Accessory Structures and Use s, Sign s, Swimming Pool s,
and Temporary Structure s and Use s unless otherwise exempted within this
Resolution.
   C)   A Zoning Permit shall not be required when any such item which has been
permitted or is otherwise legally non-conforming is being repaired or replaced
in kind unless otherwise specified within this Resolution.
   D)   A Zoning Permit shall not be required for certain items expressly
exempted within Section
117.
   E)   For permitting purposes, any project that results in the removal and
subsequent replacement, to any extent, of fifty percent (50%) or more of the
gross square footage of an existing Structure , shall be considered a new build
rather than an alteration . Such a project shall require a Zoning Permit and
shall comply with all current provisions of this Zoning Resolution, subject to
the applicable provisions of Article
25, Non-Conformities.
   F)   The Zoning Inspector shall retain the right to interpret whether a
Zoning Permit is required; however, such a decision shall be subject to appeal
to the BZA pursuant to Article
3, Section
306.
   G)   Property owners, applicants, contractors, and the like shall be
responsible for determining the exact locations of Lot Lines to ascertain no
encroachments upon another Lot . The issuance of a Zoning Permit by the Genoa
Township Development & Zoning Office does not certify the location of Lot Lines
.
115.02   Application for Zoning Permit - All Zoning Permit applications can be
obtained from the Development and Zoning Office and shall be filled out
completely prior to submission. Applications that fail to include all required
components will be considered administratively incomplete and subject to
rejection. The Township reserves the right to request revisions of submitted
materials for the purposes of demonstrating compliance, correction, accuracy,
transparency, clarification, documentation, cross-referencing, administration,
and/or enforcement. The following shall be provided as part of the application,
subject to the discretion of the Zoning Inspector:
   A)   Plans, information, materials, etc., necessary to demonstrate full
compliance with this Zoning Resolution and any applicable Legal Approval (s) in
accordance with the provisions of such.
   B)   Plans, information, materials, etc., required by any application form.
   C)   Valid authorization from the Delaware County Health Department or Ohio
Environmental Protection Agency for on-site wastewater disposal, where
applicable.
   D)   Valid authorization from the Delaware Soil and Water Conservation
District to encroach upon a drainage easement, where applicable.
   E)   Anything deemed necessary by the Zoning Inspector or their assignee to
properly administer this Zoning Resolution, including any applicable Legal
Approval (s).
   F)   A fee as established by the Township Trustees .
115.03   Processing of Zoning Permit s.
   A)   Within thirty (30) days after of receiving an administratively complete
application as determined by the Zoning Inspector or their designee, the
Development and Zoning Department shall either approve or disapprove the
application in accordance with this Resolution. If the application is approved,
the Zoning Inspector or authorized staff shall issue a Zoning Permit and
provide the applicant with either a copy of the approved permit or notice that
the application was denied. The original application shall be retained on file
by the Development and Zoning Department.
      1)   Construction authorized by a Zoning Permit shall begin within one
(1) year of issuance of the permit’s issuance. If construction does not begin
within that period, the Permit becomes invalid and must be renewed.
      2)   The ground Story framework, including structural components of any
second floor shall be completed within eighteen (18) months after Permit
issuance unless the project or Building was originally designed to be phased or
exceed eighteen (18) months in which the Zoning Inspector may authorize an
extended schedule. If required progress is not made within the applicable time
frames, the Permit becomes invalid and must be renewed.
      3)   Nothing in this Resolution shall require change to the plans,
construction , size, or designated Use of any lawful Building , Structure ,
Sign , or Swimming Pool permitted prior to the effective date of this
Resolution. When a change to such is proposed:
         a)   The Zoning Inspector may require an affidavit or similar
documentation verifying that the original intended Use of such term(s) has not
changed.
         b)   The ground Story framework, including structural components of
the second floor, shall be completed within one (1) year and the entire
improvement completed within two (2) years after the effective date of this
Resolution or its applicable amendments, subject to Section
115.03.C. Failure to meet these timeframes voids the protection provided by
this Section.
   B)   Pursuant to ORC 511.01, in the event an application involves land
within three hundred (300) feet of the centerline of a proposed new highway or
a highway for which changes are proposed as described in the certification of
local officials by the Director of the Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT)
or any land within a radius of five hundred (500) feet from the point of
intersection of said centerline with any public road or highway, the Zoning
Inspector shall give notice by registered mail to the Director of ODOT that
they shall not issue a Zoning Permit for one hundred twenty (120) days from the
date the notice is received by the Director of ODOT . If the Director of ODOT
notifies the Zoning Inspector that they shall proceed to acquire the land
needed, then the Zoning Inspector shall refuse to issue the Zoning Permit . If
the Director of ODOT notifies the Zoning Inspector that acquisition at this
time is not in the public interest or upon the expiration of the one hundred
twenty (120) day period or any extension thereof agreed upon by the Director of
ODOT and the property owner, the Zoning Inspector shall, if the application is
in conformance with all provisions of this Resolution, issue the Zoning Permit
.
   C)   When other jurisdiction permits or licenses are required, the Zoning
Inspector may request proof of such approval prior to issuing a Zoning Permit
or Certificate of Zoning Compliance .
   D)   Should the Zoning Inspector or their designee determine an application
is administratively incomplete, written notice to the applicant along with an
explanation of the application’s deficiencies shall be provided within thirty
(30) days of submittal. The Township may cease processing and reviewing the
application until the deficiencies are corrected to its satisfaction.
      1)   Should an applicant fail to resubmit a complete application within
sixty (60) days of notice being provided pursuant to Section
115.03.D, the Township may elect to not review the incomplete application. In
such case, the applicant’s original application fee shall be forfeited, the
incomplete application deemed withdrawn, no reconsideration of an incomplete
application shall occur, and a new application subject to Section
115 and this Resolution shall be required for the project to proceed. The new
application shall meet the standards in effect at the time the application is
resubmitted.
   E)   If any substantive false or misleading information is submitted or
supplied by an applicant on an application, that application may be rejected
pursuant to Section
115.03.D or denied.
115.04   Certificate of Zoning Compliance.
   A)   A Certificate of Zoning Compliance or Temporary Certificate of Zoning
Compliance shall be obtained prior to occupancy of any newly constructed
Principal Building , except where alterations or additions are otherwise
addressed within this Resolution.
      1)   The Zoning Inspector shall have the authority to require a
Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy for any other
Building , Structure , Sign , Swimming Pool , Use , improvement, activity, or
condition requiring a Zoning if deemed necessary to verify compliance with this
Resolution.
      2)   The Zoning Inspector may require supplemental documentation,
information, and/or evidence necessary to confirm zoning compliance of any
Building , Structure , Sign , Swimming Pool , Use , improvement, activity, or
property condition. Such documentation may include, but is not limited to,
certified pin location surveys, foundation surveys, as-built surveys, and
mortgage location surveys.
   B)   A Temporary Certificate of Zoning Compliance may be issued by the
Zoning Inspector for a period not exceeding eighteen (18) months during
Alterations or partial occupancy of a Building pending its completion.
115.05   The Zoning Inspector shall maintain records of all Zoning Permit s and
Certificates of Zoning Compliance and provide copies upon a valid public
records request to any person in accordance with Township policies.
115.06   Failure to obtain a Zoning Permit or any type of Certificate of Zoning
Compliance prior to commencing any required work, Use , or occupancy shall
require the submission of a late application fee, if such fee has been
established by the Township Trustees . Such failure shall also constitute a
violation of this Resolution and is subject to enforcement and penalties
pursuant to Section
116.
115.07   Conformance. Zoning Permit s or Certificates of Zoning Compliance
issued based on plans and applications approved by the Zoning Inspector
authorize only the Use and arrangement shown in such approved plans and
applications or approved amendments.
   A)   Any change to the approved Zoning Permit requires the filing of an
amendment, subject to Sections
114 and
115.01 –
115.06. An immediate late application fee may be imposed for failure to do so.
   B)   Any application for a project where the Zoning Permit has expired shall
meet the zoning standards in effect at the time the application is resubmitted.
   C)   Any Use , arrangement, or construction that deviates from the approved
plans or amendments shall be deemed a violation of this Resolution and is
subject to enforcement and penalties pursuant to Section
116.
   D)   If any substantive false or misleading information is found to have
been submitted that leads to the issuance of a Zoning Permit or any type of
Certificate of Zoning Compliance , the Zoning Inspector may revoke the Zoning
Permit ; rendering anything constructed under said document in violation of
this Resolution and subject to enforcement pursuant to Section
116.
Section 116: Enforcement
116.01   Pursuant to ORC 519.23 and 519.24, no Building , Structure , Sign , or
Use shall be established, located, erected, constructed, reconstructed,
enlarged, changed, maintained, or occupied in violation of this Zoning
Resolution, or amendment thereto. Each day a violation continues constitutes a
separate offense, regardless of whether additional notices or affidavits are
issued. The Delaware County Prosecuting Attorney, the Zoning Inspector, or any
adjacent or neighboring property owner specially damaged by such violation may,
in addition to other remedies provided by law, may institute an injunction,
mandamus, abatement, or any other appropriate legal action to prevent, enjoin
or remedy the violation. The Township Trustees may employ special counsel to
represent it in any enforcement proceedings. Violations are subject to remedies
and penalties identified within ORC 519.99, as amended.
116.02   Any applications for a Certificate of Zoning Compliance , Zoning
Permit , Conditional Use Permit , Variance , Sign permit, Temporary Use permit,
Zoning Map Amendment , Planned Development , amendment, or notice of appeal or
requests for official transcripts of hearings shall be accompanied by the
applicable fee established by resolution of the Township Trustees . No fee is
required for applications filed, or requests submitted by, any public schools
or government agencies for construction of a Government Facility. Fees imposed
under this Resolution are intended to partially offset , the administrative
costs associated with zoning review, including technical evaluations,
publishing, , and/or mailing notices, compensation of BZA or Zoning Commission
members for attendance, and other related administrative expenses. Fees are
non-refundable unless otherwise authorized by the Township Trustees .
116.03   The omission of any enforcement powers, remedy, penalty, fine or fee
authorized by law, including those specified in the ORC , shall not be
construed as a prohibiting its use. Genoa Township, the Township Trustees , the
Genoa Township Zoning Inspector, and any other legally authorized individuals,
irrespective of whether such powers are expressly sated in this Resolution.
Section 117: Exemptions from Zoning Permit s
117.01   General Provisions.
   A)   Unless otherwise specified within this Resolution or an applicable
Legal Approval , the following items are generally exempt from obtaining a
Zoning Permit . These exemptions shall not:
      1)   Exempt any item or activity from compliance with all other
applicable provisions of this Resolution;
      2)   Authorize placement of any item within a Right-of-Way ; or
      3)   Limit the authority of the Township Trustees to address Nuisance s
or take other lawful action.
   B)   The Zoning Inspector shall have the authority to determine whether a
Zoning Permit is required. Such determinations may be appealed to the Board of
Zoning Appeals pursuant to Article
3.
117.02   Exempt Items, Organized by Category, include the following:
   A)   Lighting, Décor, and Small Aesthetic Features:
      1)   Accent lighting, coach lights, and similar decorative or
architectural lighting not otherwise regulated in this Resolution.
      2)   Artwork, décor, furniture, statues, and fountains, unless:
         a)   Meeting the definition of a Structure and exceeding six (6) feet
in Height ; or
         b)   Meeting the definition of Junk , Junk Vehicle , Sign , or
Swimming Pool .
      3)   String lights, bird or bat houses, feeders, portable fountains, bird
baths, and similar small decorative features.
      4)   Flags and flagpoles, subject to applicable provisions of Article
18.
      5)   Outdoor speakers, air fresheners, repellants, traps, and similar
items not meeting the definition of a Building or Structure and not otherwise
regulated.
   B)   Small Accessory Structures and Features:
      1)   Accessory Buildings and Structure s meeting the parameters of
Article
16, Section
1609.
      2)   Decorative piers, columns, and posts not exceeding eighteen (18)
inches in width or depth and six (6) feet in Height and not attached to any
other Structure .
      3)   Portable animal coops, shelters, hives, and dog houses that do not
meet the definition of a Building , do not function as an Animal Park or
commercial Kennel , and that do not house dangerous wild animals pursuant to
Article
16, Section
1617.
   C)   Agricultural Use s:
      1)   Agriculture , Agritourism , and Farm Market s meeting the parameters
set forth in Article
23.
   D)   Governmental, Legal, and Unregulated Items:
      1)   Items expressly exempted by this Resolution, an applicable Legal
Approval , or the Ohio Revised Code, including Governmental Facilities.
      2)   Items, improvements, or Use s not expressly regulated or prohibited
by this Resolution or an applicable Legal Approval .
   E)   Pedestrian, Mobility, and Access Features:
      1)   Benches, bicycle racks, handrails, accessibility ramps, and similar
pedestrian-oriented amenities not meeting the definition of a Building .
      2)   Sidewalks, paths, trails, and other pedestrian ways.
   F)   Walls, Fences, and Boundary Features:
      1)   Fences and walls two (2) feet or less in Height ; stacked paver
walls not functioning as Retaining Wall s.
      2)   Fences surrounding tennis courts, basketball courts, or similar
facilities, provided they:
         a)   are constructed of chain-link, iron, vinyl or similar material;
         b)   are set back at least twenty (20) feet from any Front Lot Line ;
         c)   are set back at least ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot
Line ; and
         d)   are not otherwise required by this Resolution.
   G)   Driveways, Drainage, Earthwork, and Ground-Level Improvements:
      1)   Drainage infrastructure or tiles as well as driveways, basins,
berms, bridges, culverts, drains, ditches, driveways, embankments, grading,
gutters, mounds, rain barrels, or swales subject to all other applicable
regulations.
      2)   Residential driveways, driveway aprons, and parking areas compliant
with this Resolution.
      3)   Patios, boardwalks, promenades, sports courts , sports rinks, and
similar improvements constructed at grade or less than one (1) foot in height.
   H)   Recreation and Sporting Items:
      1)   Grass, dirt, or sand recreational or sporting fields not used for
commercial purposes.
      2)   Non-permanent recreational or sporting equipment including deer
stands, hunting blinds, playground equipment, playhouses, nets, bleachers,
swing sets, trampolines, treehouses, and similar items.
      3)   Permanently installed basketball hoops and other incidental, non-
commercial improvements.
   I)   Temporary, Portable, or Seasonal Items:
      1)   Certain Temporary Use s, and private garage , estate, and yard
sales, meeting Article
24, Section
2403.
      2)   Tents, cabanas, and similar portable shelters not meeting the
definition of a Structure or erected with a regulated Temporary Use .
      3)   Inflatable items not permanently affixed to the ground, including
inflatable Swimming Pool s; excluding Inflatable  Sign s prohibited by this
Resolution.
      4)   Portable grills, fire pits, torches, and similar seasonal or
temporary items.
   J)   Utility, Mechanical , and Underground Items:
      1)   Telecommunication Towers, Solar Facilities, and Wind Farms meeting
Article
22 parameters.
      2)   Propane tanks and Mechanical structures meeting Article
16, Section
1609.
      3)   Underground improvements not qualifying as a Sign , Structure , or
Swimming Pool , including electrical lines, invisible fences, plumbing, septic
systems, storm shelters, irrigation systems, wells, and similar items.
      4)   Waste, composting, and recycling receptacles that do not meet the
definition of a Portable Storage Unit or Structure .
   K)   Landscaping , Plantings, and Grounds Features:
      1)   Landscape features and amenities including:
         a)   at-grade or raised garden beds;
         b)   planting tables or potting benches six (6) feet or less in
height;
         c)   boulders; rock gardens; rain gardens;
         d)   ponds and Water Impoundments not meeting the definition of
Swimming Pool ;
         e)   plant trimming or removal not prohibited by a Legal Approval .
   L)   Repairs, Replacements, and Interior Work:
      1)   Repair or replacement in-kind of improvements constructed under a
valid Zoning Permit or otherwise legally non-conforming, per Article
25.
      2)   Roof repairs and interior renovations occurring entirely within a
Structure , except window wells regulated under Article
16, Section
1608.04.
   M)   Home Occupations meeting certain parameters as set forth in Article
16, Section
1618.
   N)   Sign s meeting certain parameters as further Set forth in Article
18, Sections
1802 and
1803.
ARTICLE 2: Responsibilities of the Zoning Commission
Section 201: Township Zoning Commission
201.01   The Township Trustees shall establish a Zoning Commission , in
accordance with ORC 519.04, consisting of five (5) citizens of the Township
appointed by the Township Trustees . Up to two (2) additional citizens may be
appointed as alternates. No member or alternate may concurrently serve as a
member of the Township Trustees , BZA, or Architectural Review Board (if so
established).
201.02   Terms shall be arranged so that the term of one member expires each
year. Each member shall serve until their successor is appointed and qualified.
201.03   Pursuant to ORC 519.04.B, members of the Zoning Commission shall be
removable for nonperformance of duty, misconduct in office, or other cause by
the Township Trustees , upon written charges being filed with the Township
Trustees , after a public hearing has been held regarding the charges, and
after a copy of the charges has been served upon the member so charged at least
ten (10) days before the hearing, either personally, by registered mail or by
leaving the copy at the member’s usual place of residence. The hearing shall
occur within sixty (60) days after the charges are filed. The member shall be
given an opportunity to be heard and answer the charges. Upon the approval of a
majority of the Township Trustees , the member may be suspended from
participating as a member of the Zoning Commission during the period of up to
sixty (60) days before the pending hearing on the removal. Vacancies shall be
filled by the Township Trustees and shall be for the unexpired term. A
suspension authorized by this section is not a vacancy for purposes of this
section. The decision of the Township Trustees regarding the suspension or
removal may be appealed under ORC 2506.
201.04   The Zoning Commission shall elect its own officers annually and adopt
rules for the conduct of its affairs consistent with this Resolution (i.e.,
Rules of Procedure). The Commission shall meet as needed, but not less than
quarterly at the call of the Chair or as determined by the Zoning Commission .
The Chair, or Acting Chair, may administer oaths and compel the attendance of
witnesses. All meetings shall be open to the public.
201.05   The Zoning Commission shall keep minutes of its proceedings and
records of all examinations and other official actions. All of which shall be
public record.
201.06   The Zoning Commission shall act by resolution or motion. A majority
vote of a quorum of Zoning Commission members shall be necessary to pass any
resolution or motion, as well as to recommend the approval, disapproval, or
modification of any proposed amendment to this Resolution. In the case of the
latter, such actions shall be forwarded to the Township Trustees unless
otherwise provided in this Resolution.
201.07   The Zoning Commission shall possess all powers and authorities granted
by the ORC , including the authority to initiate proposed amendments to this
Resolution and/or Zoning Map and make recommendations to the Township Trustees
in accordance with Article
26 or Article
27. All such actions shall follow applicable provisions of the ORC and this
Resolution.
201.08   The Zoning Commission shall also review all proposed Preliminary
Development Plan Text s, Final Development Plan s, and Final Development Plan
amendments and make recommendations to the Township Trustees in accordance with
Article
27 and ORC 519.05. The Zoning Commission shall have decision-making authority
regarding Final Development Plan amendments deemed by the Commission to be
minor amendments in accordance with the provisions of this Resolution, as
further described in Article
27.
ARTICLE 3: Responsibilities of the Board of Zoning Appeals
Section 301: Board of Zoning Appeals
301.01   The Township Trustees shall establish a Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA),
in accordance with ORC 519.13, consisting of five (5) residents of the Township
appointed by the Township Trustees . Up to two (2) additional alternates may be
appointed. No member or alternate may concurrently serve as a member of the
Township Trustees, Zoning Commission , or Architectural Review Board (if so
established).
301.02   Terms shall be arranged so that the term of one member expires each
year. Each member shall serve until their successor is appointed and qualified.
301.03   Pursuant to ORC 519.13.B, members of the Board of Zoning Appeals may
be removable for nonperformance of duty, misconduct in office, or other cause
by the Township Trustees , upon written charges being filed with the Township
Trustees, after a public hearing has been held regarding the charges, and after
a copy of the charges has been served upon the member so charged at least ten
(10) days before the hearing, either personally, or by registered mail, or by
leaving the copy at the member’s usual place of residence. The hearing shall
occur within sixty (60) days after the charges are filed. The member shall be
given an opportunity to be heard and answer the charges. Upon the approval of a
majority of the Township Trustees , the member may be suspended from
participating as a member of the Board of Zoning Appeals during the period of
up to sixty (60) days before the pending hearing on the removal. The decision
of the Township Trustees regarding the suspension or removal may be appealed
under ORC 2506. Vacancies shall be filled by resolution of the Township
Trustees and shall be for the unexpired term. A suspension authorized by ORC
519.04 is not a vacancy for the purposes of this section.
301.04   The Board of Zoning Appeals shall adopt rules necessary for the
conduct of its affairs consistent with this Resolution (i.e., Rules of
Procedure). Meetings shall be held at the call of the Chair or as otherwise
determined by the BZA. The Chair, or in their absence the Acting Chair, may
administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses.
301.05   All meetings shall be open to the public. The BZA shall keep minutes
of its proceedings, including the vote of each member upon question or if
indicate of absence/non-voting, and its examinations and other official
actions. All such records shall be public records and shall be filed in the
office of the BZA.
301.06   Pursuant to ORC 519.14 and Sections
302 –
307 of this Resolution, the BZA has the following specific responsibilities:
   A)   Hear and decide appeals where it is alleged there is error in any
order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative
official in the enforcement of ORC 519.02 to 519.25, or of any resolution
adopted pursuant thereto.
   B)   Authorize, upon appeal, in specific cases, such Variance from the terms
of the Zoning Resolution as will not be contrary to the public interest, where,
owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the resolution will
result in unnecessary hardship, and so that the spirit of the resolution shall
be observed and substantial justice done.
   C)   Grant conditional zoning certificates (i.e., Conditional Use Permits )
for the use of land, Building s, or other Structure s if such certificates for
specific Use s are provided for in the Zoning Resolution. If the BZA considers
conditional zoning certificates for activities that are permitted and regulated
under ORC 1514 or activities that are related to making finished aggregate
products, the BZA shall proceed in accordance with ORC 519.141.
   D)   Revoke an authorized Variance or conditional Zoning Certificate for the
extraction of Minerals , if any condition of the Variance or certificate is
violated.
      1)   The BZA shall notify the holder of the Variance or certificate
either by certified mail or, if the board has record of an internet identifier
of record (as defined in ORC 9.312) associated with the holder, by ordinary
mail and by that internet identifier of record of its intent to revoke the
Variance or certificate under ORC 519.14.D and of the holder's right to a
hearing before the BZA, within thirty (30) days of the mailing of the notice,
if the holder so requests. If the holder requests a hearing, the BZA shall set
a time and place for the hearing and notify the holder. At the hearing, the
holder may appear in person, by the holder's attorney, or by other
representative, or the holder may present the holder's position in writing. The
holder may present evidence and examine witnesses appearing for or against the
holder. If no hearing is requested, the BZA may revoke the variance or
certificate without a hearing. The authority to revoke a variance or
certificate is in addition to any other means of zoning enforcement provided by
law.
   E)   Pursuant to ORC 519.14, in exercising its duties, the BZA may, in
conformity with the terms of this Resolution, reverse or affirm, wholly or
partly, or modify the order, requirement, decision, or determination appealed
from and may make such order, requirement, decision, or determination as ought
to be made, and to that end shall have all powers of the officer from whom the
appeal is taken.
301.07   The BZA may also determine the exact location of any District boundary
in accordance with Section
503.
301.08   A majority vote of a quorum of the BZA is required to reverse any
order, requirement, decision, or determination of the Zoning Inspector, or to
decide in favor of the applicant on any matter the BZA is required to address
under this Resolution.
301.09   The Zoning Commission and Township Trustees shall not have authority
over the responsibilities assigned to the BZA, nor shall they have the
authority to assume such responsibilities or override any decision of the BZA.
301.10   Decisions made by the Township Trustees or the Zoning Commission shall
not be appelable to the BZA. Decisions of the BZA likewise are not appealable
to the Township Trustees or Zoning Commission .
301.11   The BZA may enter private deliberations with legal counsel during any
quasi-judicial proceedings; however, all decisions shall be rendered in an open
session unless otherwise permitted by law.
301.12   The BZA, subject to Section
301.06.E, may reconsider its own decision until the institution of a court
appeal or the expiration of the applicable appeal period.
301.13   Individuals providing testimony before the BZA are subject to cross-
examination.
301.14   Applications to the BZA are subject to the doctrine res judicata.
Section 302: Conditional Use s
302.01   Certain Use s within Genoa Township are permitted only through a
Conditional Use review and approval process, as established in this Resolution
and identified within Article
5.
302.02   An application for Conditional Use approval by at least one (1) owner
of the property is required prior to any authorization by the Board of Zoning
Appeals . At a minimum, the application shall contain the following
information:
   A)   Plans, information, and materials demonstrating compliance with this
Zoning Resolution, including applicable Conditional Use standards and Legal
Approval (s).
   B)   Plans, information, materials, etc., required by any application form.
   C)   Anything deemed necessary by the Zoning Inspector or their assignee to
properly administer this Zoning Resolution, including any applicable Legal
Approval (s); and
   D)   A fee as established by the Township Trustees .
302.03   The Board of Zoning Appeals may waive, implicitly or explicitly, any
Conditional Use submittal requirement herein with the exception of the required
application fee.
Section 303: Conditional Use Provisions
303.01   Conditional Use s may be approved only when the proposed Use is found
to comply with the standards of this Resolution and all other applicable
requirements. Nothing in this Section, however, shall be interpreted to
guarantee approval of Conditional Use merely because all such standards are met
303.02   Conditional Use regulations and specific Conditional Use standards
shall be as set forth in Article
17 unless otherwise stated.
Section 304: Conditional Use Procedures
304.01   The BZA shall hold a public hearing within a reasonable time after
receiving a complete Conditional Use application.
   A)   Public notice of the hearing shall be provided by any method authorized
by the ORC at least ten (10) days prior to the hearing date. Such notice shall
state the time, place, and nature of the public hearing .
   B)   Written notice of such hearing shall be mailed by the Zoning Inspector
or their designee, by first class mail, at least ten (10) days prior to the
hearing to the parties in interest including the owners of property Contiguous
to and directly across the street from the applicant’s property. The applicant
shall provide a list of such property owners and one set of pre-addressed,
legal-size envelopes, with sufficient postage. These shall be used by the
Township to issue mailed notices. Mailed notices shall contain the same
information required for published notices.
304.02   Within a reasonable time after the hearing, the BZA shall approve,
approve with supplementary conditions, or disapprove the application. If the
BZA disapproves the application, such decision being an administrative act made
in an adjudicative setting, may be appealed by the applicant to the Court of
Common Pleas.
Section 305: Conditional Use Permit
305.01   If a Conditional Use is approved, the applicant shall subsequently
apply for and obtain a Conditional Use Permit (i.e., Zoning Permit ) prior to
establishing the approved Use. Except as otherwise provided in this Resolution,
Conditional Use Permits are subject to the provisions of Sections
115 (Zoning Permit s and Certificates of Compliance ) and
116 (Enforcement).
305.02   A Conditional Use Permit shall be deemed to authorize only one
particular Conditional Use . The Conditional Use Permit shall automatically
expire if, for any reason, the Conditional Use shall cease for more than six
(6) months, or if construction or establishment is not begun within twelve (12)
months of approval of the Conditional Use Permit .
   A)   Should a Conditional Use Permit expire for any reason, a new
Conditional Use Permit pursuant to the standards, procedures, and provisions of
Sections
302 –
304 shall be required to be established. Applications shall meet the zoning
standards in effect at the time the application is resubmitted and shall be
required to pay all applicable fees.
Section 306: Administrative Appeals
306.01   In accordance with ORC 519.15, appeals to the BZA regarding
the interpretation or administration of this Resolution may be filed by any
person aggrieved or affected by a decision made by any administrative officer
of the Township.
306.02   An appeal shall be filed within twenty (20) days of the decision being
appealed by submitting a written notice to the Township. This notice shall
specify the grounds for the appeal. The Zoning Inspector shall transmit to the
BZA all the papers constituting the record upon which the action appealed was
taken.
306.03   The filing of an appeal stays all proceedings related to the action
appealed unless the Zoning Inspector certifies to the BZA that, due to specific
stated facts, a stay would cause imminent peril to life or property. In such
cases, proceedings shall not be stayed except by a restraining order that may
be granted by BZA or by a court of record on application, on notice to the
Zoning Inspector from whom the appeal was taken.
306.04   The BZA shall set a time and place for the appeal hearing and shall
provide at least ten (10) days’ written notice to all parties in interest,
including the owners of property Contiguous to and directly across the street
from the applicant’s property. Public notice of hearings, including its date,
place, and subject matter, shall also be published by any method authorized by
the ORC at least ten (10) days before the hearing date. Any party in interest
may appear and be heard at the hearing in person, by agent, or by attorney.
306.05   The BZA shall have all the powers of the Zoning Inspector with respect
to the decision under appeal. A concurring vote of a majority of a quorum of
BZA members is required to reverse or modify any decision of the Zoning
Inspector. The BZA shall issue a written decision and finding of fact without
unreasonable delay after the close of a hearing. A copy of the decision and
findings of fact shall be sent to the Township Trustees and Zoning Commission ,
and by certified mail to the applicant.
306.06   A notice of appeal shall be accompanied by the applicable fee
established by the Township Trustees .
Section 307: Variance s
307.01   A Variance to any standard within this Zoning Resolution may be
requested by any individual or party. Such a request shall be considered and
decided by the BZA. Denial of a Zoning Permit or any type of Certificate of
Zoning Compliance shall not be a prerequisite to make such an application.
307.02   No Variance shall be granted unless the applicant submits a written
Variance application to the Township and provides sufficient evidence
demonstrating a requested Variance is warranted under the standards of this
Resolution as determined by the BZA.
307.03   An application for a Variance shall contain, at a minimum, the
following information:
   A)   Plans, information, and materials demonstrating compliance with this
Zoning Resolution, including applicable Conditional Use standards and Legal
Approval (s).
   B)   Plans, information, materials, etc., required by any application form.
   C)   Anything deemed necessary by the Zoning Inspector or their assignee to
properly administer this Zoning Resolution, including any applicable Legal
Approval (s); and
   D)   A fee as established by the Township Trustees .
307.04   The BZA may waive, implicitly or explicitly, any Variance submittal
requirement herein with the exception of the required application fee.
307.05   Approval of a Variance . The applicant bears the burden of proving
that a Variance request should be approved. Except as otherwise provided for
Area Variance s in Section
307.06 and Use Variance s in Section
307.07 below, the BZA shall only approve a Variance , or modification thereof,
if the following findings are made by the BZA:
   A)   That such Variance or modification will not be contrary to the public
interest;
   B)   That owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of this Zoning
Resolution will result in unnecessary hardship; and
   C)   That the approval of such Variance or modification thereof is
consistent with the spirit of this Zoning Resolution, and substantial justice
shall be done thereby.
307.06   Area Variance s. The BZA shall not grant an Area Variance unless the
Board determines that the applicant has encountered practical difficulties in
the use of the subject property. The BZA shall consider all relevant factors in
determining whether the applicant has encountered practical difficulties in the
use of such property, including, but not limited to:
   A)   Whether the property in question will yield a reasonable return or
whether there can be any beneficial use of the property without the Variance .
   B)   Whether the Variance is substantial.
   C)   Whether the essential character of the neighborhood would be
substantially altered, or whether adjoining properties would suffer a
substantial detriment as a result of the variance.
   D)   Whether the Variance would adversely affect the delivery of
governmental services (e.g., water, sewer, garbage, emergency response,
maintenance of public infrastructure).
   E)   Whether the property owner purchased the property with knowledge of the
zoning restriction.
   F)   Whether the property owner's predicament feasibly can be obviated
through some method other than a Variance .
   G)   Whether the spirit and intent behind the zoning requirement would be
observed and substantial justice done by granting the Variance .
307.07   Use Variance s. The BZA shall not grant a Use Variance unless an
unnecessary hardship exists as determined by the BZA. An unnecessary hardship
shall exist only if the applicant is able to sufficiently prove, with facts, to
the Board that it is not economically feasible to put the subject property to
any Use permitted within its current zoning classification due to
characteristics unique to the property. An unnecessary hardship shall be
considered to not exist if the property is suitable for any Use permitted
within its current zoning classification.
307.08   The BZA shall hold a public hearing within a reasonable time after the
receiving an application for a Variance . Public notice of the hearing provided
by any method authorized by the ORC at least ten (10) days prior to the hearing
date. The notice shall set forth the date, time, place, and the nature of the
hearing.
307.09   Written notice of the public hearing shall be mailed by the BZA
Township, by first class mail, at least ten (10) days prior to the hearing to
the parties in interest including all owners of property Contiguous to and
directly across the street from the applicant’s property. The applicant shall
provide a list of such property owners and one set of pre-addressed, legal-size
envelopes with sufficient postage. These shall be used by the Township to issue
mailed notices. Mailed notices shall contain the same information required for
published notices.
307.10   Conditions. In granting any Variance request, the BZA may prescribe
appropriate conditions and safeguards in conformity with this Resolution.
Violation of such conditions and safeguards, when made a part of the terms
under which the request for a Variance is granted, shall be deemed a violation
of this Resolution and thus subject to enforcement pursuant to Section
116.
307.11   The BZA shall have all the powers of the Zoning Inspector with respect
to such decision. The concurring vote of a majority of a quorum of BZA members
shall be necessary to reverse or modify any decision of the Zoning Inspector.
The BZA shall issue a decision based on findings of fact on the application
without unreasonable delay after the closure of a hearing. A copy of the
decision shall be sent to the applicant.
307.12   Expiration of Approval. Unless otherwise stipulated by the BZA, the
applicant for a Variance shall obtain a Zoning Permit for the proposed project
within one (1) year of the approval being granted; otherwise, the approval
shall lapse, expire, and be null and void ab initio.
   A)   Extensions of time may be requested by the applicant in writing by
filing such a request with the Zoning Inspector at least thirty (30) days prior
to the expiration of the one (1) year period. If an applicant fails to make an
extension request within the prescribed deadline, the approved Variance shall
become void, and a new Variance would have to be sought. Subsequent extension
requests shall also be subject to this protocol.
   B)   The BZA, for good cause shown, may enlarge the one (1) year period
prescribed within this Section.
   C)   Alternatively, when approving a Variance , the BZA has discretion to
grant the Zoning Inspector the authority to extend said Variance . Requests
would be subject to the deadline established in Section
307.12.A.
ARTICLE 4: Definitions
Section 401: Introduction
401.01   All words, terms, abbreviations, and/or phrases used in this
Resolution shall retain their customary meanings as defined in Webster’s New
World: College Dictionary, Fourth Edition, 2009, published by Wiley Publishing,
Inc., unless otherwise specifically defined within this Resolution. An
exception to this being any technical words and phrases not otherwise defined
in this Zoning Resolution that may have acquired a peculiar and appropriate
meaning in law, in which case such words and phrases shall be construed and
understood according to such meaning.
Section 402: Definitions
Accessory Building or Structure – A Building or Structure located on the same
Lot or Tract as an associated Principal Structure that: contains a lawful
Accessory Use ; and/or is designed, arranged, intended, maintained, or occupied
in a manner that is customarily incidental and subordinate in area, extent, or
purpose to the Principal Building or Structure which it serves (e.g., Accessory
Dwellings , decks, Detached garages, Fences, gazebos, pavilions, sheds,
Swimming Pool s, walls, etc.).
Accessory Storage – The incidental keeping of goods, materials, and other such
items directly related to a Principal Use on the same property, regardless of
whether said storage occurs within a Principal Structure or an Accessory
Structure .
Accessory Telecommunications – Telecommunications Tower s between eight (8)
feet and thirty-five (35) feet in Height , including Distributed Antenna
Systems (DAS) and small cells sites, communication nodes, antennas, fiber-optic
cables, radio transceivers, and any additional equipment associated with
transmission, which are typically used to supplement the service of larger
Telecommunications Tower s and reduce the need for additional larger
Telecommunications Tower s.
Accessory Use – Any purpose for which a Building , Structure , or a portion of
land may be designed, arranged, intended, maintained, or occupied which is
customarily ancillary, incidental, and/or subordinate in area, extent or
purpose to a Principal Use that is located on the same Lot or Tract .
Accessory Wall – An Accessory Structure consisting of any vertical wall, taller
than one (1) foot, which is not constructed to retain soil or other natural
materials.
ADA – The Americans with Disabilities Act.
Addition – An improvement that increases the area and/or Height of a Structure
, including: those which extend laterally to the front, side, or rear of a
Structure, those which extend vertically on top of a Structure, and/or
enclosures added underneath an above ground Structure but shall not include any
improvements being made underneath and underground of an existing Structure so
long as it does not expand the existing, above ground footprint of said
Structure.
Adult Use Cannabis Operations – Any and all activities or operations described
as such by ORC 3780 or 3796, as may be amended (i.e., Adult Use Cannabis
Operators).
Agricultural Production – See ORC 901.80(A)(1) and 929.01(A), as may be
amended.
Agriculture – Any and all activities recognized by ORC 519.01 and/or 519.21, as
may be amended.
Agritourism – Any and all activities recognized in ORC 519.01, 519.21(D)(2),
and/or 901.80(A)(2), as may be amended.
Alteration – Any change in the supporting members (such as bearing walls,
beams, columns, roof structure, or girders) of a Building , Sign , Structure ,
or Swimming Pool , any addition to the exterior of a such, or any movement of
such from one location to another. This definition shall not include the repair
or replacement of any such item in kind.
Amateur Radio Service Communications – Any and all activities recognized by ORC
519.214, as may be amended.
Amphitheater – A fully or quasi outdoor space specifically designed and built
to enable an audience to observe competitions, performances, productions, and/
or motion pictures on a set, stage, and/or screen generally situated on one end
of the facility, including but not necessarily limited to band shells and
drive-in theaters.
Amusement Arcade – Any commercial establishment where six (6) or more Amusement
Devices are located, but which does not otherwise operate as a Games of Chance
Establishment .
Amusement Device – Any mechanical , electrical, digital, and/or virtual machine
or apparatus used to for entertainment and/or the playing of games, which may
be commonly known as “pinball machines”, “video games”, “virtual reality”, or
“jukeboxes”, or upon which games and/or music played after the insertion of a
coin or other disc, slug, or token for which fees paid to any kind of an
attendant. This definition shall include any technological successors, both
known and unknown.
Amusement Park – A permanently sited establishment where patrons typically pay
a fee to enjoy rides regulated by the Ohio Department of Agriculture, Division
of Amusement Ride Safety & Fairs, and which may also feature Amusement Devices,
exhibitions, games of skill or chance, performances, and the like. Such Use may
also contain within its confines Arena s, Amphitheater s, Auditorium s,
Drinking Establishment s, Event Facilities , Food Halls, Galleries, Mobile
Vending , Museums, Nightclubs, Open Space , Restaurant s, Retail Establishment
s, Stadium s, and/or other similar types of Use s which customarily provide
food, refreshments, recreation, entertainment, and/or operations support.
Amusement Resort – An establishment featuring two (2) or more separately-
ticketed Amusement Park (s), an Amusement Park in conjunction with a Hotel ,
and/or an Amusement Park in combination or conjunction with any other separate
Principal Use which may or may not be located within the former’s confines
including administrative, maintenance, safety, transportation, and/or utility
facilities needed to properly run and support such an operation.
Anemometer – An instrument that measures the force and direction of the wind.
Animal Park – An establishment which maintains a collection of animals (wild or
domestic), including dangerous wild animals as defined and regulated by ORC
935.01(C), as may be amended, typically in a park, garden, or tank, for study,
conservation, and/or display to the public; commonly known as an aquarium,
menagerie, safari park, petting zoo, and/or zoo. Such a facility may contain
facilities necessary to support the operation.
Animal Shelter – See ‘Kennel ’.
Antenna, Aerial – An arrangement of wires or metal rods used in sending or
receiving electromagnetic waves. Antennas may be freestanding or affixed to
Building s. They are supported in the air by a Structure used primarily for
supporting one or more antennas, including foundation, guys, and other
components thereof. For the purpose of this Resolution, telecommunications
towers as defined in ORC 519.211(B)(1) shall not be considered an Aerial
Antenna but shall be regulated in accordance with the provisions of Section
2204 of this Resolution.
Arena – A completely indoor facility specifically designed and built to enable
an audience to observe athletic events, competitions, performances,
productions, and/or motion pictures occurring in a space surrounded on most or
all sides by seating for spectators, also commonly referred to as a coliseum or
fieldhouse.
Attached – Any Structure or part of a Structure immediately adjacent to another
Structure or part of a Structure and fastened securely to the same. When
Attached is used to define the connection of two (2) Building s, they must
either:
   A)   Share a Common Wall ; or
   B)   Provide for internal access between the two (2) Building s.
Auction House – An establishment used to auction (in person, remotely, or via
the internet) goods, materials, and property, both new and used, that is stored
and/or displayed on-site, including aircraft, automobiles, Commercial Motor
Vehicle s, motorcycles, Off-Road Motorized Vehicles , recreational vehicles
(RVs), campers, and trailers (travel and hauling). Such Use shall also include
any facilities primarily used to store, repair, refinish, and/or refurbish such
items.
Auditorium – A completely indoor facility specifically designed and built to
enable an audience to observe competitions, performances, productions, and/or
motion pictures on a set, stage, and/or screen generally situated on one end of
the room, such as, but not necessarily limited to, concert venues,
entertainment studios that admit an audience, movie theaters, and performance
halls.
Automobile Detail – Any Building , Structure , Lot , Tract , or portion thereof
used to render on-site services involving the detailing of motor vehicles,
excluding Commercial Motor Vehicle s, including buffing, striping, painting,
finishing, interior cleaning, glass repair, audio/visual installation, and
audio/visual repair but shall include any services meeting the definition of
Automobile Repair .
Automobile Fueling/Charging Station – A non-residential facility that is
primarily arranged, designed, used, or intended to be used to sell and dispense
fuel and/or energy for motor vehicles, excluding Marinas. Such establishments
may also contain Ancillary  Retail and/or a Restaurant functioning as an
Accessory Use , but do not include any Use which primarily meets the definition
of, and functions as, a Truck Terminal .
Automobile Repair – Any Building , Structure , Lot , Tract , or portion
thereof, in/upon which a business or industry performs or renders an on-site
service (s) involving the maintenance, servicing, and/or repairing of motor
vehicles, including quick-change services but excluding Commercial Motor
Vehicle s, but not otherwise meeting the definition of Automobile Detail .
Automobile Salvage – See ‘Junkyard ’.
Automobile Wash – Any Building , Structure , Lot , Tract , or portion thereof,
primarily utilized for washing motor vehicles and/or Heavy Equipment .
Aviation Facility – Any privately owned Building , Structure , Lot , Tract , or
portion thereof, which contains one or more of the following; Landing Pads,
Landing Strips, runways, moorings, hangars, terminals, concourses, fueling
stations, and the like or any other Structure s, equipment, improvement, or
open space utilized to operate, track, repair, rent, lease, sell, test, store,
detail, or wash aircraft or spacecraft and/or any such related components,
including private airports. This definition shall also include the rental of
space for the storage of the aforementioned but shall exclude incidental
