Section 1744: Fleet Maintenance Facility
1744.01   All service work and repair shall be done inside an enclosed Building
. No outdoor dismantling, wrecking, or storage of automotive vehicles or parts
shall be permitted unless otherwise expressly permitted by this Resolution.
1744.02   Fuel pumps and vacuums shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the Front Lot Line and ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot Line .
1744.03   When such Use is located within a Residential Zoning District (where
permitted), garage, repair bays, fuel pumps, and vacuums shall be screened by
an opaque, decorative Fence six (6) feet in Height .
1744.04   When such Use is located within a Non-Residential Zoning District ,
garages, repair bays, fuel pumps, and vacuums shall not face any Street or Lot
within the Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District unless screened
or separated from such by another Building or an opaque, decorative Fence six
(6) feet in Height .
1744.05   Such Use shall not be permitted to operate as an Automobile Salvage
or a Junkyard . No derelict, damaged, unlicensed vehicles, or Junk Vehicles
shall be stored on the premises for more than forty-eight (48) hours.
1744.06   Vehicles awaiting repair outside, as well as wrecked vehicles and
Junk Vehicles , shall be screened, and a view of them from adjacent Lots and
streets shall be obscured with a solid vegetative landscape buffer or opaque
fencing of at least six (6) feet in height.
1744.07   When vehicles are to be stored on the site awaiting repair, there
shall be a designated storage area that shall not include the required parking
space for the site. Such storage shall not cause traffic hazards or the
blocking of traffic flow.
1744.08   All storage of new, used, or discarded parts or materials shall be
within a fully enclosed Structure .
1744.09   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.

Section 1747: Food Preparation, Processing, Packaging, and/or Wholesale Plants
1747.01   The following standards shall apply to Food Preparation/Wholesale

   B)   The minimum required Lot size for such a Use shall be five (5) acres.

Section 1748: Games of Chance Establishment
1748.01   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
1748.02   Games of Chance Establishment s are permitted as a Principal Use only
in the Zoning Districts expressly specified within this Zoning Resolution and
shall be subject to the following restrictions:
   A)   Games of Chance Establishment s shall not be permitted within one
thousand (1,000) feet, as measured from the closest Lot Line of each Use ,
unless otherwise specified, of any: Dwelling within a Residential or Planned
Residential Zoning District ; other Games of Chance Establishment ; Cemetery ,
Crematorium , Funeral Home , or Mortuary ; Cultural Center ; Day Care Centers
(all types); Educational Institutions (grades 12 or lower); Hospital ; Natural
Resource Protection area; Public library or Museum ; Public park or playground;
or Religious Establishment .
   B)   Only one (1) Games of Chance Establishment is permitted in a single
Structure when such Use is established as Principal Use . No co-location of
principal Games of Chance Establishments shall be permitted within one (1)
Structure .
   C)   All gaming activity shall occur within the confines of a fully enclosed
Building . For the purpose of this section, covered decks, covered patios,
covered Porch es, three-season rooms, and other such spaces shall not be
considered a fully enclosed Building .
   D)   Illicit material shall not be displayed publicly.
1759.03   All operations must be conducted within an enclosed Building ; doors
and windows shall remain closed during hours of operation. For the purpose of
this section, covered decks, covered patios, covered Porch es, three-season
rooms, and other such spaces shall not be considered a fully enclosed Building
.
1759.04   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1759.05   No Games of Chance Establishment shall feature any components meeting
the definition of a Sexually Oriented Business .
Section 1749: Golf Course
1749.01   Golf Course s in Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District s
shall only be permitted when they are subsidiary to the primary residential Use
of the property.
1749.02   All Structure s, Game Fields/Courts , Swimming Pool s, and other such
facilities that are not solely used for storage or mechanics (e.g.,
electricity, plumbing, etc.) shall be set back at least one hundred (100) feet
from the Front Lot Line and fifty (50) feet from all other Lot Lines adjacent
to the subject Lot or Tract . All other Structure s shall be set back at least
twenty-five (25) feet from any Lot Line adjacent to the subject Lot or Tract .
1749.03   All maintenance equipment shall be stored in sheds or other Structure
s and away from view.
1749.04   No hole or green shall be located within two hundred (200) feet of an
existing Residential Type Use unless otherwise approved as part of a larger
Planned Development District, so long as said residences are also part of the
Planned Development .
1749.05   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided.
1749.06   The minimum Floor Area requirements for the clubhouse or management
Structure shall be five thousand (5,000) square feet.
1749.07   Any Golf Course s hereinafter constructed within designated areas of
Genoa Township shall occupy not less than one hundred fifty (150) acres.
1749.08   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1749.09   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1749.10   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500)
feet of any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall cease
between the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This
provision shall not apply to incidental activities or routine maintenance of
such facilities.
Section 1750: Home Occupation , Low-Impact
1750.01   When Conditional Use approval is desired or required by this
Resolution for a Home Occupation , the following standards shall apply:
   A)   There shall be no more than two (2) non-residential employees or
volunteers to be engaged in the proposed Use ;
   B)   Sales of commodities not produced on the premises may be permitted
provided that the commodities are specified in the application, are reasonably
related to the Home Occupation , and are sold within the interior of a Building
(i.e., Outdoor Displays are prohibited) or a Structure as permitted in Sections
2303.03 and
2303.04;
   C)   Outside Storage related to the Home Occupation may be permitted if
totally screened from adjacent residential Lots pursuant to Section
1610.05, provided the application specifies;
   D)   Not more than thirty percent (30%) of the gross Floor Area of any
residence shall be devoted to the proposed Home Occupation ; however, up to
100% of a lawful and otherwise permitted Accessory Building may be devoted to
the proposed Home Occupation ;
      1)   Any Accessory Building containing a Home Occupation , existing or
proposed, shall be in full and complete compliance with this Zoning Resolution,
subject to Article
25, Non-Conformities.
   E)   The external appearance of the Structure in which the Use is to be
conducted shall not be altered, and not more than one (1) Sign no larger than
two (2) square feet shall be mounted flush to the wall of the Structure ;
   F)   Minor or moderate Alterations in accordance with other provisions of
this Resolution may be permitted to accommodate the proposed Use but there
shall be no substantial construction or reconstruction;
   G)   No equipment process, materials, or chemicals shall be used that create
offensive noise, vibration, smoke, dust, odor, heat, glare, X-rays, radiation,
or electrical disturbances; and
   H)   No more than two (2) additional parking places may be proposed in
conjunction with the Home Occupation . Such spaces shall not be located in the
required Front Yard .
   I)   Exterior lighting related to the Home Occupation shall conform with the
provisions of Article
21 with the exception of exterior Porch , patio, garage, and/or garden lighting
fixtures, including carriage lights and yard lamps, that are customary to
Single-Family Dwelling s.
Section 1751: Hospitals and Large Medical Clinics
1751.01   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
1751.02   Vehicular Access.
   A)   Hospital s situated on Lots or Tract s less than twenty (20) acres in
area shall have direct vehicular access to at least one (1) Arterial Street .
   B)   Hospital s situated on Lots or Tract s of twenty (20) acres or more in
area shall have direct vehicular access to one (1) Arterial Street and one (1)
Collector Street or two (2) access points on an Arterial Street . The minimum
required separation distance of the latter shall be three hundred (300) feet
between access points, subject to the approval of the Delaware County Engineer.
   C)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
1751.03   A drop-off/pick-up area separate from any designated parking areas
shall be provided so that the parking of vehicles being used for such purpose
can occur adjacent to the Building site without requiring pedestrians to walk
through a parking lot or the blocking of any parking spaces, ingress/egress
points, emergency access ways, mail delivery locations, or waste collection
service areas.
1751.04   Internal Access Street System. A looping internal access Street
system shall be provided. All Use s shall have access by means of the internal
access Street system. The internal Street system shall be arranged to allow
proper development of the surrounding properties and a continuous network with
the internal Street systems of surrounding properties.
1751.05   Pedestrian Circulation. A system of Pedestrianway s, sidewalks,
crossings, and the like shall be provided for access to the center along and
across access Streets and from adjacent residential Use s, as well as for
access within the center.
1751.06   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1751.07   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1751.08   Any such Use containing a Landing Pad/Strip shall also comply with
the standards set forth herein for such Use as well as with the standards set
forth herein for Aviation Facilities.
1751.09   Any such Use that contains a Day Care Center shall also comply with
the standards set forth herein for Day Care Center Establishments .

1752.02   A drop-off/pick-up area separate from any designated parking areas

Section 1753: Junkyards and Landfills/Incinerators
1753.01   Standards set forth within this Article for Automobile Salvage shall
apply to Junkyards.
1753.02   The following standards shall apply to Landfills/Incinerators:
   A)   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
   B)   The Use shall not be located on a Lot with Frontage on an Arterial
Street but shall be located on a Lot accessed from a Street with direct access
to an Arterial Street .
   C)   Landfills/Incinerators shall be located at least one thousand (1,000)
feet from any adjoining Residential Type Use , Planned Residential Zoning
District , or Residential Zoning District .
   D)   The perimeter of the Lot or Tract containing such Use shall be screened
in accordance with Section
2003.
   E)   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor Storage
areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete
pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to
protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
   F)   A description of the nature, character, logistics, timing, duration,
and impacts of the proposed operation, including:
      1)   The location of areas on site which will be utilized for storage of
materials and/or waste as well as the manner in which storage shall occur.
      2)   The location of any facilities that will be utilized for the
processing, loading, and/or transportation of materials or waste.
      3)   How lighting and/or glare will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare. Outdoor
lighting, if any, shall be shielded and/or reflected away from adjoining
properties.
      4)   How dust and/or debris will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
      5)   How noise and/or vibrations will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
      6)   How fumes and/or odor will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
      7)   How diminution and pollution of air, land, and/or water, including
above and below ground water supplies, will be prevented to the greatest extent
possible to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare.
   G)   A list of materials or products that could decompose by detonation
shall be provided to the Genoa Township Fire Department. Such materials shall
include, but need not be limited to, all primary explosives including lead
oxide and lead sulfate; all high explosives and boosters such as TNT, RDS,
tetryl, and ammonium nitrate; propellants and components thereof such as
nitrocellulose, black powder, ammonium perchlorate and nitroglycerin; blasting
explosives such as dynamite, powdered magnesium, potassium chlorate, potassium
permanganates, and potassium nitrate, and nuclear fuels and reactor elements
such as uranium 235 and plutonium.
   H)   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .

Section 1759: Mobile Enterprise  Use s
1759.01   The following standards shall apply to Use s meeting the definition
of Mobile Enterprise :
   A)   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
   B)   The Use shall have the permission of the property owner to operate.
Documentation of such proof shall be provided when a Legal Approval is
required. This standard shall not apply to Mobile Enterprises operating in a
public Street , those operating as part of a larger Temporary Event, and those
occupying spaces designated for such Use in an approved Final Development Plan
.
   C)   With the exception of lawful Temporary Events, no more than two (2)
Mobile Enterprises may operate on a Lot in a Straight Zoning District at any
one time.
   D)   Mobile Enterprises on private property shall be set back at least fifty
(50) feet from any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District unless
screened by an on-site Fence at least five (5) feet in Height in which case the
setback shall be reduced to ten (10) feet. This standard shall not apply to
Mobile Service Businesses providing services on-site to a singular client.
   E)   Mobile Enterprises shall not park on any non-paved area within a
designated Open Space area or required Front Yard .
   F)   The Use , including any of its associated components, amenities, or
activities, shall not block any Streets , Right-of-Way s, accessible parking
spaces, emergency access routes, clear sight triangles, road or utility
easements, Pedestrianway s, or any other clearance zones that may be required
by other governmental agencies. This restriction shall not apply to any such
features located within a conventional parking space, driveway, or other
similar type of area that could equally be blocked by a standard motorized
vehicle.
   G)   Electrical cords, water hoses, etc., crossing such areas shall be
securely covered to prevent tripping, hazards, and damage to vehicles.
   H)   Supplies and any other items related to the operation of the Mobile
Enterprise shall be stored within the interior of the vehicle or trailer where
the operation is occurring or within an enclosed Building . No such items shall
be stored outside.
   I)   A letter from the Genoa Township Fire Department approving the proposed
location of the Mobile Enterprise shall be provided prior to the issuance of a
Legal Approval .
   J)   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
   K)   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500) feet
of any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall cease between
the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This standard
shall not apply to Mobile Service Businesses providing services on-site to a
singular client.
   L)   Waste, including debris, Junk , litter, refuse, and trash, as well as
compost and recyclables, including grease and grey water, shall be controlled,
stored in proper containers, handled, and disposed of in accordance with the
requirements of the Delaware Public Health District and any other agency having
jurisdiction over such matters.
   M)   Mobile Vending Business es shall be subject to the regulations and/or
restrictions of any Legal Approval applicable to the Lot or Tract on which they
are operating. In the instance of conflict, the stricter shall apply.
1759.02   The following standards shall apply to Use s meeting the definition
of Mobile Enterprise Court :
   A)   Mobile Enterprises occupying the facility shall comply with Section
1759.01 above.
   B)   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided. No such facility shall be
located within one hundred (100) feet of a Lot or Tract located within a
Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District .
   C)   A centralized dumpster, four (4) cubic yards in size, shall be
provided.
      1)   The dumpster shall not be located within one hundred (100) feet of a
Lot or Tract located within a Residential or Planned Residential Zoning
District .
      2)   Screening of the dumpster shall be provided in accordance with
Article
20, Section
2004.03.
1759.03   The following standards shall apply to both Mobile Enterprises and
Mobile Enterprise Court s:
   A)   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500) feet
of any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall cease between
the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This provision
shall not apply to incidental activities or routine maintenance of such
facilities.
   B)   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor Storage
areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete
pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to
protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
   C)   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to these Use s.
Section 1760: Mobile Home Use s
1760.01   The following standards shall apply to Mobile Homes:
   A)   Mobile Homes shall only be permitted in an approved Mobile Home Park .
   B)   Mobile Homes shall comply with all applicable standards set forth
herein for Mobile Home Park s.
   C)   The placement of a Mobile Home within an approved Mobile Home Park
shall be considered a Use by right and shall not require Conditional Use
approval.
1760.02   The following standards shall apply to Mobile Home Park s:
   A)   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
   B)   The location of all Mobile Home Park s shall comply with the following
minimum requirements:
      1)   Minim Lot or Tract size: Ten (10) Contiguous acres.
      2)   Such a Use shall not be established wholly or partially on an
existing wetland even if mitigation is proposed.
      3)   Such a Use shall not be located in a Regulatory Flood Plain .
   C)   Mobile Home Park Design Requirements.
      1)   All required Landscaping shall comply with the provisions of Article
20, Section
2002.
      2)   The perimeter of the Mobile Home Park shall be screened in
accordance with Article
20, Section
2003.02.
      3)   Stormwater infrastructure shall be screened in accordance with
Article
20, Section
2003.06
      4)   Off-Street Parking lots shall be screened in accordance with Article
20, Section
2004.01.
      5)   Building s shall be landscaped in accordance with Article
20, Section
2004.02.
      6)   Dumpsters and the like shall be screened in accordance with Article
20, Section
2004.03.
      7)   Building mechanicals shall be landscaped in accordance with Article
20, Section
2004.04.
      8)   Grades and slopes shall be landscaped in accordance with Article
20, Section
2004.05.
      9)   All required plantings shall comply with the species and size
requirements set forth in Article
20, Sections
2005 and
2006.
   D)   Mobile Home Lot Design Requirements.
      1)   All Mobile Home Lot s shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the exterior boundaries of the Mobile Home Park .
      2)   The minimum area of any Mobile Home Lot shall be at least six
thousand (6,000) square feet.
      3)   The subject area of the Mobile Home Lot shall be improved to provide
an adequate foundation for the placement of the Mobile Home in such a position
as to allow a minimum of fifteen (15) feet between the Mobile Home and any
adjacent Street  Right-of-Way .
      4)   Individual Mobile Homes, including Accessory Structures  attached
thereto, shall be set back at least thirty (30) feet from one another. This
requirement shall not restrict attachments as long as a minimum separation of
twenty (20) feet.
      5)   Individual Mobile Homes, including Accessory Structures  attached
thereto, shall be set back at least fifteen (15) feet from internal Streets or
common areas.
   E)   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor Storage
areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete
pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to
protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
   F)   No part of any Mobile Home Park shall be used for a Non-Residential
Type Use except for such Use s required for the direct servicing of the public
health and safety of the park’s residents or the management and maintenance of
the park.
   G)   No central toilet or washroom facilities shall be permitted.
   H)   Pumps, including those for fuel, wastewater, and/or greywater, shall be
set back at least fifty (50) feet from any Lot Line .
   I)   Vehicle repair, service, and/or maintenance facilities shall comply
with the standards set forth within this Article for Vehicle Sales, Rental, and
Service .
   J)   Nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to prohibit the sale
of a Mobile Home located on a Mobile Home Lot connected to utilities.
   K)   Exterior lighting shall conform with the provisions of Article
21 with the exception of exterior Porch , patio, garage, and/or garden lighting
fixtures, including carriage lights and yard lamps, that are customary to
Single-Family Dwelling s.
   L)   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .

Section 1762: Multi-Family Building s
1762.01   The following standards shall be specific to Multi-Building
Complexes:
   A)   The site shall have vehicular access to an Arterial and/or Collector
Street .
      1)   The minimum required separation distance between access points on
the same Street shall be three hundred (300) feet, subject to the approval of
the Delaware County Engineer.
      2)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
   B)   In addition to Article
19, the following parking standards shall apply:
      1)   Parking lots shall be designed so that at least one standard semi-
trailer can be parked off-street adjacent to any Building containing a Dwelling
without blocking any parking spaces, ingress/egress points, emergency access
ways, mail delivery locations, or waste collection service areas.
      2)   Parking spaces shall be located no more than three hundred (300)
feet from the entrance of the Building that the spaces are intended to serve.
   C)   A paved pedestrian network of sidewalks, trails, paths, and designated
crosswalks shall be provided to provide connected, non-motorized routes between
all Building s within the complex.
1762.02   The following standards shall be specific to Multi-Family –
Multiplexes:
   A)   In addition to Article
19, the following parking standards shall apply:
      1)   Parking spaces shall be located no more than one hundred (100) feet
from the entrance of the Building the spaces are intended to serve.
1762.03   The following standards shall apply to both Multi-Family – Complexes
and Multi-Family Multiplexes:
   A)   All dumpster, compost/recycling/waste collection, and/or trash
compactor areas shall be located at least fifty (50) feet from the closest
Dwelling and enclosed by a solid, decorative masonry wall at least six (6) feet
in Height . The number and size of such areas shall be enough to service the
entire complex without creating a hazard to public health or safety. The
vehicular access needed to service such area(s) shall be designed so that no
servicing vehicle blocks any parking spaces, ingress/egress points, emergency
accessways, primary Pedestrianway s, or mail delivery locations.
   B)   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor Storage
areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete
pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to
protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
   C)   Exterior lighting shall conform with the provisions of Article
21 except for exterior Porch , patio, garage, and/or garden lighting fixtures,
including carriage lights and yard lamps, that are customary to Single-Family
Dwelling s.
   D)   If a Swimming Pool is proposed as part of the Use , the Standards set
forth in this Article for Swimming Pool s shall apply.
Section 1763: Natural Resource Extraction
1763.01   Surface mining activities authorized via Conditional Use in this
Zoning Resolution shall be processed, reviewed, and considered in accordance
with ORC 519.141.
1763.02   This Use shall be subject to Section
1702.05.
1763.03   A description of the nature, character, logistics, timing, duration,
and impacts of the proposed operation, including:
   A)   The material(s) being extracted.
   B)   The purpose(s) for extraction.
   C)   A map(s) identifying the area and extent of the proposed activity.
   D)   A site plan(s) illustrating the area and extent of the proposed
activity as well as the location and design of all proposed Structure s and
equipment, regardless of whether they are permanent, temporary, or transient.
   E)   The proposed depth(s) of exaction.
   F)   The location of areas on site which will be utilized for storage of
materials and/or waste, as well as the manner in which storage shall occur.
   G)   The location of any facilities that will be utilized for the
processing, loading, and/or transportation of materials or waste.
   H)   How materials and waste will be transported on and/or off-site,
including:
      1)   Anticipated route(s) of travel.
      2)   Number of vehicles to be used for transport.
      3)   Arid weight of vehicles to be used for transport.
      4)   Maintenance plans for any Street used for transport.
   I)   How lighting and/or glare will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare. Outdoor
lighting, if any, shall be shielded and/or reflected away from adjoining
properties.
   J)   How dust and/or debris will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
   K)   How noise and/or vibrations will be mitigated to the greatest extent
possible to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
   L)   How fumes and/or odor will be mitigated to the greatest extent possible
to protect public health, safety, and general welfare.
   M)   How diminution and pollution of air, land, and/or water, including
above and below ground water supplies, will be prevented to the greatest extent
possible to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare.
   N)   Plans and intentions for the restoration and reclamation of all land
affected by the operation to a condition that will support reasonable
utilization of the site by any Use permitted by the applicable Zoning District
as set forth in Article
5.
   O)   Primary contact information for the operation.
   P)   Emergency contact information for the operation.
1763.04   The processing of extracted materials in any manner on-site shall be
prohibited unless such processing is necessary for proper transport and/or to
ensure public safety.
1763.05   In order to grant Conditional Use approval for this Use , the Board
of Zoning Appeals shall require sufficient information to determine that:
   A)   The scale, pace, and duration of the proposed activity are reasonable
in relation to the ability of other portions of Genoa Township to maintain
normal patterns of activity while extraction is occurring.
   B)   Adequate safeguards are provided to ensure that damage will not be done
to property elsewhere in Genoa Township or the natural environment.
   C)   The proposed plan for reclamation and reuse of land is acceptable and
in compliance with this Zoning Resolution. If the proposed reclamation is for
Agriculture , forestry, Natural Resource Protection , and/or any other type of
undeveloped Use , grading, drainage, and vegetation shall be compatible with
other similar Use s in Genoa Township.
1763.06   In order to grant Conditional Use approval or a modified Conditional
Use approval for the expansion or change of such Use , the Board of Zoning
Appeals shall require sufficient information to determine that:
   A)   The performance of the applicant and/or Use has been in conformance
with all Legal Approvals, including any prior Conditional Use approval(s).
   B)   No expansion in the area of such Use shall be permitted until
extraction activities have been completed on an equivalent area of land and
said land shall have been graded, vegetated, and otherwise established in
accordance with any Legal Approvals pertaining to the reclamation of the site,
including any prior Conditional Use approval(s).
1763.07   The scope, area(s), and method(s) of extraction shall not exceed or
be larger and/or more intense than those licensed and/or permitted by any
applicable state and/or federal permitting authorities for such Use .
1763.08   A permanently placed Sign identifying the name of the operator,
materials being extracted, contact information of the operator, and emergency
contact information of the operator shall be posted at each access point onto
the site. Such signage shall not count towards signage otherwise permitted by
Article
18. The following provisions shall also apply:
   A)   The Sign shall be reasonably visible and legible from adjacent Internal
Streets .
   B)   The Sign shall be set back no less than ten (10) feet and no more than
twenty (20) feet from any adjoining Street .
   C)   The Sign (s) shall have a Sign Area of no less than ten (10) square
feet and no more than twenty (20) square feet.
   D)   The total width of the Sign shall not exceed seven and one-half (7 ½)
feet.
   E)   The Sign shall have a total height of no less than four (4) feet and no
taller than eight (8) feet.
1763.09   A list of materials or products that could decompose by detonation
shall be provided to the Genoa Township Fire Department. Such materials shall
include, but need not be limited to, all primary explosives including lead
oxide and lead sulfate; all high explosives and boosters such as TNT, RDS,
tetryl, and ammonium nitrate; propellants and components thereof such as
nitrocellulose, black powder, ammonium perchlorate and nitroglycerin; blasting
explosives such as dynamite, powdered magnesium, potassium chlorate, potassium
permanganates, and potassium nitrate, and nuclear fuels and reactor elements
such as uranium 235 and plutonium.
1763.10   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided.
1763.11   Should any provisions herein conflict with any applicable state and/
or federal law or agency, the stricter shall apply.
Section 1764: Nightclub
1764.01   No Nightclub shall be established within five hundred (500) feet,
measured Lot Line to Lot Line , from another Nightclub or from any: Dwelling
within a Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District ; Cemetery ,
Crematorium , Funeral Home , or Mortuary ; Cultural Center ; Day Care Centers
(all types); Educational Institutions (grades 12 or lower); Hospital ; Natural
Resource Protection area; public library or museum ; public park or playground;
Religious Establishment ; Sexually Oriented Business ; or Substance Abuse
Treatment Clinic .
1764.02   Facility entrances and exits (excluding emergency exits) facing a
Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall have a vestibule with
a second door to minimize noise.
1764.03   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1764.04   The owner and operator must provide adequate private security
licensed under the laws of the State of Ohio during events that attract maximum
permitted occupancy.
1764.05   All operations must be conducted within an enclosed Building ; doors
and windows shall remain closed during hours of operation. For the purpose of
this section, covered decks, covered patios, covered Porch es, three-season
rooms, and other such spaces shall not be considered a fully enclosed Building
.
1764.06   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1764.07   No Nightclub shall feature any components meeting the definition of a
Sexually Oriented Business .
Section 1765: Nursery , Retail or Wholesale
1765.01   Impervious Surfaces shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Lot
Area .
1765.02   Greenhouse  Structure s shall be set back at least one hundred (100)
feet from any Lot Line adjoining the subject Lot or Tract .
1765.03   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided.
1765.04   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1765.05   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances. This standard shall not apply to aisleways between rows of
plantings.
1765.06   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1765.07   Nurseries, Retail or Wholesale, with a Building of over twenty
thousand (20,000) square feet, a mixture of Building s and Structure s totaling
more than twenty thousand (20,000) square feet, and/or on a Lot or Tract one
(1) or more acre in size shall also adhere to the standards set forth for Large
Retail Establishment s set forth herein this Article.
Section 1766: Off-Road Motorized Vehicle Track
1766.01   Standards set forth within this Article for Recreation and/or
Instructional Facility , Outdoor shall apply.
1766.02   Fuel pumps and vacuums shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the Front Lot Line and ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot Line .
1766.03   Vehicle repair, service, and/or maintenance facilities shall comply
with the standards set forth within this Article for Vehicle Sales, Rental, and
Service .
1766.04   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided.
1766.05   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1766.06   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500)
feet of any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall cease
between the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This
provision shall not apply to incidental activities or routine maintenance of
such facilities.
Section 1767: Office - Large
1767.01   Vehicular Access.
   A)   Any such Use situated on Lots or Tract s less than twenty (20) acres in
area shall have direct vehicular access to at least one (1) Arterial Street .
   B)   Any such Use situated on Lots or Tract s twenty (20) acres or more in
area shall have direct vehicular access to one (1) Arterial Street and one (1)
Collector Street or two (2) access points on an Arterial Street . The minimum
required separation distance of the latter shall be three hundred (300) feet
between access points, subject to the approval of the Delaware County Engineer.
   C)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
1767.02   Internal Access Street System. A looping internal access Street
system shall be provided. All Use s shall have access by means of the internal
access Street system. The internal Street system shall be arranged to allow
proper development of the surrounding properties and a continuous network with
the internal Street systems of surrounding properties.
1767.03   Pedestrian Circulation. A Pedestrianway system shall be provided for
access to the center along and across access Streets and from adjacent
residential Use s, as well as for access within the center.
1767.04   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1767.05   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1767.06   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
Section 1768: Oil and Gas Production
1768.01   Standards set forth within this Article for Natural Resource
Extraction shall apply unless otherwise exempt as further specified in Article
1, Section
102.10 of this Resolution.
Section 1769: Outdoor Collection
1769.01   The provisions within this Section shall not apply to Outdoor
Collection receptacles placed temporarily or seasonally for a period of thirty
(30) consecutive days or less. Such receptacles may be placed by right without
obtaining Legal Approval .
1769.02   The Use shall have the permission of the property owner to operate.
Documentation of such proof shall be provided when a Legal Approval is
required. This standard shall not apply to Mobile Enterprises operating on a
public Street or as part of a larger Temporary Event.
1769.03   No more than one (1) Outdoor Collection receptacle shall be permitted
on a Lot or Tract .
1769.04   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall not be permitted within a
designated Open Space area or a required Front Yard .
1769.05   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall only be permitted on paved
surfaces such as asphaltic concrete or Portland cement concrete pavement.
1769.06   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall be set back at least fifty (50)
feet from any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District .
1769.07   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall not block any Streets , Right-
of-Way s, required parking spaces, required parking drive aisles, emergency
access routes, clear sight triangles, road or utility easements, Pedestrianway
s, or any other clearance zones that may be required by other governmental
agencies. If such a receptacle is placed along a Pedestrianway , five (5) feet
of clearance shall be always maintained.
1769.08   Outdoor Collection receptacles that are not placed adjacent to a
Building shall be screened from the view of neighboring properties and Streets
pursuant to the standards set forth in Section
2004 of this Resolution.
1769.09   Maintenance.
   A)   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall be designed to prevent the
overflow or blowing away of materials.
   B)   Any materials left outside of the overflow receptacle shall be
deposited within the receptacle or collected from the site within seven (7)
days.
   C)   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall be maintained in good physical
condition, with no broken, chipped, fading, loose, missing, peeling, or rusted
exteriors or components, and otherwise free of Deterioration, decomposition,
and/or decay.
   D)   The failure to adhere to these standards shall be grounds for the
revocation of the Legal Approval permitting the Use and/or grounds for
enforcement pursuant to Article
1 Section
116 of this Resolution.
1769.10   The name and contact information of the owner of the Outdoor
Collection receptacle shall be clearly and legibly displayed on the receptacle.
1769.11   Outdoor Collection receptacles shall be subject to the regulations
and/or restrictions of any Legal Approval applicable to the Lot or Tract on
which they are operating. In the instance of conflict, the stricter shall
apply.
Section 1770: Parking Facility
1770.01   The site shall have direct vehicular access to an Arterial and/or
Collector Street .
   A)   The minimum required separation distance between access points on the
same Street shall be three hundred (300) feet, subject to the approval of the
Delaware County Engineer.
   B)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
1770.02   The maximum grade of parking floors shall not exceed six percent
(6%).
1770.03   The maximum grade of ramps shall be:
   A)   Covered; Fifteen percent (15%).
   B)   Uncovered: Twelve percent (12%).
1770.04   For multilevel facilities, at least one (1) elevator shall be
provided for each two hundred and fifty (250) parking spaces.
1770.05   Parking space and associated drive aisle dimensions shall comply with
the provisions of Article
19.
1770.06   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1770.07   The facility shall be designed so that pedestrians utilizing the
primary entrance/exit do not have to step into or traverse through any
designated parking space, drive aisle, or vehicular access point.
1770.08   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1770.09   Any outdoor, surface-level parking area shall also comply with the
standards set forth within this Article for Off-Street Parking Lot .
Section 1771: Parking Lot, Off-Street
1771.01   The following standards shall only apply when an Off-Street Parking
Lot is being proposed as a Principal Use :
   A)   The Use shall not be located on a Lot with Frontage on an Arterial or
Collector Street when being proposed or established as a Principal Use .
   B)   The facility shall be designed so that pedestrians utilizing the
primary entrance/exit do not have to step into or traverse through any
designated parking space, drive aisle, or vehicular access point.
   C)   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor Storage
areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete
pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to
protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
   D)   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .

1772.01   Standards set forth within this Article for Recreation and/or

1772.02   Fuel pumps and vacuums shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the Front Lot Line and ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot Line .
1772.03   Vehicle repair, service, and/or maintenance facilities shall comply
with the standards set forth within this Article for Vehicle Sales, Rental, and
Service .
1772.04   Facilities housing, training, or caring for animals shall comply with
the standards set forth within this Article for Recreation and/or Instructional
Facilities , Outdoor.
1772.05   Collected animal waste shall not be stored within five hundred (500)
feet of the perimeter of the subject Lot or Tract .
1772.06   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected

1772.08   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500)

between the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This
provision shall not apply to incidental activities or routine maintenance of

Section 1773: Recreation and/or Instructional Facility , Outdoor
1773.01   Minimum Lot Area or Tract size shall be no less than five (5) acres.
1773.02   Access and Traffic Impact - Access shall be from an Arterial Street
or a Collector Street . The minimum required separation distance between access
points on the same Street shall be three hundred (300) feet, subject to the
approval of the Delaware County Engineer.
1773.03   Setback s:
   A)   Front: 100 feet for structures and 75 feet for parking;
   B)   Rear: 75 feet; and
   C)   Side: 75 feet.
   D)   Driveways and parking areas shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District .
1773.04   All outdoor playing fields, courts , and other similar outdoor
recreation facilities must be secured at night to prevent unauthorized access.
1773.05   Exterior lighting shall conform to the provisions of Article
21.
1773.06   No more than eighty percent (80%) of the Lot or Tract area may
comprise of outdoor fields, courts , rinks, and the like.
1773.07   A minimum eight (8) foot high landscaped screen or combination mound
and plant material with a ninety percent (90%) year-round opacity shall be
provided on any side of the site containing an outdoor amenity that is adjacent
to Lots within a Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District . If a
mound is used, it shall be constructed with no more than a 4 to 1 slope. Mounds
shall not be constructed to restrict the natural flow of surface water to or
from the site.
1773.08   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1773.09   Permanent restroom facilities located within a Building and connected
to a sanitary sewer or other approved on-site disposal system approved by the
Delaware Public Health District must be provided.
1773.10   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas, other than those intended to house animals, shall be hard-
surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement concrete pavement, permeable
pavement, or another suitable alternative that is proven to protect surrounding
properties and activity from dust and other disturbances.
1773.11   Ranges and courses used for shooting and throwing sports (e.g., guns,
bows, darts, axes, knives, paintball, airsoft, archery tag, laser tag, etc.)
shall comply with all provisions established for such within Section
1723 (Commercial and/or Private Recreational Facilities ) of this Article.
1773.12   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1773.13   Outdoor operations of any such facility within five hundred (500)
feet of any Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District shall cease
between the overnight hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. This
provision shall not apply to incidental activities or routine maintenance of
such facilities.
1773.14   Racetrack s and Swimming Pool s shall comply with the provisions set
forth for such Use (s) within this Article.
Section 1774: Religious Establishment
1774.01   Unless expressly approved as part of a Planned Development in a
Planned Zoning District , the Lot containing any standalone Religious
Establishment shall have Frontage on and direct vehicular access to an Arterial
Street or Collector Street as further designated by the current Delaware County
Thoroughfare Plan .
   A)   The minimum required separation distance between access points on the
same Street shall be three hundred (300) feet, subject to the approval of the
Delaware County Engineer.
   B)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
1774.02   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1774.03   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1774.04   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1774.05   A Private Educational Institution (s) shall be permitted on the same
Lot or Tract as a Religious Establishment so long as such Use (s) do not
comprise more than twenty (20) acres of the subject Lot or Tract , inclusive of
any associated parking area. The following standards shall also apply:
   A)   When the associated Religious Establishment is located within a
Straight District, Conditional Use approval pursuant to Article
3 shall be obtained.
   B)   When the associated Religious Establishment is located within a Planned
Zoning District , it shall be subject to the provisions of Article
27.
   C)   Accessory Dwellings in all Zoning Districts shall also comply with the
standards set forth herein for Accessory Dwelling s.
1774.06   No more than one (1) Accessory Dwelling shall be permitted on the
same Lot or Tract as a Religious Establishment . The following standards shall
also apply:
   A)   When the associated Religious Establishment is located within a
Straight District, Conditional Use approval pursuant to Article
3 shall be obtained.
   B)   When the associated Religious Establishment is located within a Planned
Zoning District , it shall be subject to the provisions of Article
27.
   C)   Accessory Dwellings in all Zoning Districts shall also comply with the
standards set forth herein for Accessory Dwelling s.
1774.07   Any such Use that contains a Day Care Center shall also comply with
the standards set forth herein for such Use .
1774.08   Any such Use that contains a Cemetery shall also comply with the
standards set forth herein for such Use .
Section 1775: Residential Care Facilities
1775.01   Pursuant to ORC 5119.341(B), Residential Care Facilities of six (6)
or more residents (excluding caregivers) are prohibited in certain Zoning
Districts as further identified in Article
5, Section
505: Table of Authorized Principal Uses .
1775.02   Residential Care Facilities shall obtain a Zoning Permit prior to
commencing the use of a property as a Residential Care Facility .
1775.03   In order to promote the benefits of residential surroundings for the
residents of Residential Care Facilities and to further the goal of
deinstitutionalization of persons whose disabilities or status limit their
ability to live independently and to foster their integration into the
mainstream of society, no Residential Care Facility housing six (6) or more
residents (excluding caregivers) shall be located within 1,320 feet of any
other such Residential Care Facility .
   A)   Genoa Township may, in accordance with the procedures and provisions of
this Zoning Resolution, issue a Conditional Use Permit , or, in the case of a
Planned Development , grant a Divergence , for such a facility to locate within
1,320 feet of another facility upon a finding that:
      1)   The residents of said facility will benefit from normal residential
surroundings;
      2)   The placement within 1,320 feet of another Residential Care Facility
does not hinder the goal of deinstitutionalization;
      3)   The placement of the Residential Care Facility furthers the goal of
integrating the residents into the mainstream of society;
      4)   A hardship exists in that suitable housing is unavailable elsewhere
in the community that meets the 1,320-foot spacing requirement;
      5)   The architectural design and site layout of the proposed facility
and the location, nature, and Height of any walls, screens, and Fences shall be
compatible with adjoining land uses and the character of the neighborhood; and
      6)   The proposed facility shall fully comply with all Yard , parking,
and Sign regulations and shall comply with all health, fire, and safety
regulations and building standards.
1775.04   Service meals shall be limited to residents only.
1775.05   A loading/unloading area separate from any designated parking areas
shall be provided so that the parking of vehicles being used for such purpose
can occur adjacent to the Building without blocking any parking spaces,
ingress/egress points, emergency access ways, mail delivery locations, or waste
collection service areas.
1775.06   Exterior lighting shall conform with the provisions of Article
21 with the exception of exterior Porch , patio, garage, and/or garden lighting
fixtures, including carriage lights and yard lamps, that are customary to
Single-Family Dwelling s.
1775.07   If a Swimming Pool is proposed as part of the Use , the Standards set
forth within this Article for Swimming Pool s shall apply.
Section 1776: Retail Establishment , Large
1776.01   The site shall have Frontage on and direct vehicular access to a
Major Arterial Street as further designated by the current Delaware County
Thoroughfare Plan .
   A)   Any such Use situated on Lots or Tract s less than twenty (20) acres in
area shall have direct vehicular access to at least one (1) Arterial Street .
   B)   Any such Use situated on Lots or Tract s twenty (20) acres or more in
area shall have direct vehicular access to one (1) Arterial Street and one (1)
Collector Street or two (2) access points on an Arterial Street . The minimum
required separation distance of the latter shall be three hundred (300) feet
between access points, subject to the approval of the Delaware County Engineer.
   C)   Direct vehicular access to a Local Street shall be prohibited.
1776.02   A traffic report shall be submitted with the application for
development which identifies traffic control measures within the site and at
the points of ingress and egress warranted at peak usage of the facility.
1776.03   Site Layout Standards.
   A)   Where adjacent Internal Streets , driveway connections, and/or
Pedestrianway s are existing, approved, or proposed by a public, quasi-public,
and/or private entity, connection to such features in kind shall be required.
   B)   Where Off-Street Parking is arranged perpendicular to aisle ways
collecting traffic, a planting or landscaped island shall be required at the
intersection of interior collector aisle ways. Such an island shall begin
parallel with the last parking space or spaces at the end of a row of parking
spaces and not occupy space assigned to the aisle way itself.
   C)   A circuitous network of Pedestrianway s shall be provided. Such ways
shall also provide a connection to any existing or proposed Pedestrianway s
along or adjacent to the development.
   D)   Landscaped curb bulb-outs shall be provided wherever a Pedestrianway
crosses an Internal Street or parking drive aisle.
1776.04   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1776.05   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1776.06   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1776.07   Building Layout Standards.
   A)   Designated loading and delivery areas should be separated from parking
lots and associated vehicular circulation.
   B)   Loading and delivery for such Use s that do not have designated loading
and delivery areas shall be allowed from any side of the Building .
1776.08   Architectural Guidelines. The following item(s) are not required, but
are strongly encouraged:
   A)   There should be no blank or bare exterior walls for more than thirty-
five (35) linear feet (measured horizontally) where the wall is visible from a
Street , parking lot, or Pedestrianway . Blank or bare walls should have an
element constructed within them that creates a visual break in the wall;
examples are faux windows, pilasters, or other such permanent architectural
features achieving the effect.
Section 1777: Sales, Rental, and Service  Use s, Building s, Vehicles or
Watercraft
1777.01   The standards set forth herein shall apply to the following Use s:
Commercial Motor Vehicle  Sales, Rental, and Service ; Manufactured, Mobile, or
Recreational Building /Vehicle Sales, Rental, and Service ; Vehicle Sales,
Rental, and Service ; and Watercraft Sales, Rental, and Service .
1777.01   Such Use s shall not be located on a Lot with Frontage on an Arterial
Street but shall be located on a Lot accessed from a Street with direct access
to an Arterial Street .
1777.02   All operations other than parking, display, and fueling exclusively
for crafts, equipment, machines, vehicles, etc., being sold, rented, or and/or
displayed, shall occur within a fully enclosed Building . No outdoor
dismantling, wrecking, or storage of such, including parts, shall be permitted
unless otherwise expressly permitted by this Resolution. These provisions
include, but are not necessarily limited to, detailing and repair.
1777.03   All storage of new, used, or discarded parts or materials shall be
within a fully enclosed Structure except for tires, which shall be permitted to
be stored outside in accordance with the provisions of Article
16, Section
1610.
1777.04   Berths, garage bays, loading bays, and repair bays shall not face any
Street or Lot within the Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District
unless separated from such by another Building or screened in accordance with
Sections
2003 and
2004.
1777.05   Fuel pumps and vacuums shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the Front Lot Line and ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot Line .
1777.06   Such Use shall not be permitted to operate as an Automobile Salvage
or a Junkyard . No derelict, damaged, Junk Vehicles , or unlicensed vehicles
shall be stored outside on the premises for more than forty-eight (48) hours.
1777.07   Buffer areas shall be provided in accordance with the following:
   A)   Perimeter Landscaping . A minimum forty (40) foot wide landscape strip
shall be provided around the perimeter of the site with five (5) evergreen
trees having a height of not less than six (6) feet per thirty-five (35) linear
feet of perimeter. In addition, an elevated earth berm a minimum of five (5)
feet higher than the finished elevation of the parking lot(s) shall be
provided. Where existing vegetation occurs along the perimeter of the lot line,
a fifty (50) foot wide undisturbed preservation strip having existing mature
trees may be substituted for the required planting(s).
1777.08   All Structure s shall be set back a minimum of one hundred (100) feet
from the Front Lot Line .
1777.09   No portion of the Lot shall be paved with asphalt, concrete, or other
substance within seventy-five (75) feet from the Right(s)-of-Way adjoining such
Lot or Tract .
1777.10   A designated storage area shall be provided for any item on the site
awaiting detailing, repairing, servicing, washing, etc. Parking spaces required
by Article
19 shall be utilized for this purpose nor shall they satisfy this requirement.
1777.11   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
proven to protect surrounding properties and activity from dust and other
disturbances.
1777.12   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
1777.13   Any portion of the Use meeting the definition of Automobile Detail ,
Automobile Repair , Automobile Fueling/Charging Station , Automobile Wash ,
Large Retail Establishment , Parking Facility , Transportation Services and
Facilities , Truck Terminal , and/or Warehouse shall comply with the standards
set forth herein for such Use s. When standards conflict, the stricter shall
apply unless otherwise stated.
1777.14   The following standards shall only apply to Watercraft Sales, Rental,
and Service  Use s:
   A)   This Use shall also comply with the standards within this Article for
Outdoor Recreation and/or Instructional Facility .

1778.01   Standards set forth within this Article for Heavy Equipment  Sales,
Rental, and Service shall apply.
Section 1779: Sales, Rental, and Service , Heavy Equipment
1779.01   The Use shall not be located on a Lot with Frontage on an Arterial

1779.02   Loading bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the Residential
or Planned Residential Zoning District unless separated from such by another
Building or screened in accordance with Sections
2003 and
2004.
1779.03   Fuel pumps and vacuums shall be set back at least fifty (50) feet
from the Front Lot Line and ten (10) feet from any Side or Rear Lot Line .
1779.04   Vehicle repair, service, and/or maintenance facilities shall comply
with the standards set forth within this Article for Vehicle Sales, Rental, and
Service .
1779.05   Noise Control standards of Section
1702.06 shall apply to this Use .
Section 1780: Sales, Rental, and Service , Machine
1780.01   The Use shall not be located on a Lot with Frontage on an Arterial
Street but shall be located on a Lot accessed from a Street with direct access
to an Arterial Street .
1780.02   Garage and repair bays shall not face any Street or Lot within the
Residential or Planned Residential Zoning District unless screened or separated
from such by another Building or an opaque, decorative Fence eight (8) feet in
Height .
1780.03   The ground surface of any parking, driving, loading, or Outdoor
Storage areas shall be hard-surfaced with asphaltic concrete, Portland cement
concrete pavement, permeable pavement, or another suitable alternative that is
